Serbian student coalition brings down strongman Vučić in electoral upset. But no PM in sight

The student-led victory in Serbia is expected to reverberate across Europe, adding momentum to youth and student protests that have shaken governments across the continent.

Debdutta Chakraborty

26 October, 2026 07:02 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Supporters of the electoral list 'Student List - Students Win' celebrate after Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in the parliamentary election in Belgrade, Serbia | REUTERS/Uros Arsic

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

New Delhi: In an unprecedented electoral upset in the Balkans, a student-led coalition brought down the far-right’s decade-old hold on Serbia. But no one knows who the next Prime Minister will be. Far right leader Aleksandar Vučić lost to a student-led movement in snap elections Sunday in what is being called a new political era in Belgrade.

The electoral outcome followed an extraordinary period of protests against corruption and government negligence, culminating in a pivotal moment that resulted in a voter turnout reported to be the highest in 30 years.

Vučić, who was PM for three years from 2014 to 2017 and President for nine years since then, conceded defeat after more than a decade of political dominance as the student-led movement won a decisive majority in the country’s 250-seat parliament.

Show Full Article

The election became, in effect, a referendum on Serbia’s political future: whether the country would continue under Vučić’s Serbian Progressive Party, known as the SNS, or a movement promising to restore democratic institutions, strengthen the rule of law and confront corruption. The youth-backed Students’ List, will take between 135 and 140 seats. The SNS got 105 seats.

Following Vučić’s resignation in September, Serbian Parliament Speaker Ana Brnabić assumed presidential duties. Vučić claimed he stepped down to contest the 25 October parliamentary election in a bid to become prime minister. Serbia must now hold presidential elections in the coming months to elect a successor and determine who will serve as the country’s next head of state.

The student movement, meanwhile, began in 2024 with students blockading streets after a concrete canopy collapsed outside the railway station in Novi Sad, Serbia’s second-largest city, killing 16 people.

Within less than two years, it grew into a nationwide campaign that brought together people from across Serbian society, including farmers, actors, judges, academics and other citizens disillusioned with the government.

The students had no obvious leaders and little conventional political experience. Yet their ‘Student List—Students Win’ movement attracted anti-government voters across the country. They fielded candidates for all 250 parliamentary seats, but no students appeared on the list. For now, they have not announced their PM candidate.

Serbia’s former President and Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) prime ministerial candidate Aleksandar Vucic concedes defeat during the parliamentary election in Belgrade, Serbia | REUTERS/Zorana Jevtic The victory marked a reversal for Vučić, an ultranationalist who cultivated an image as a pragmatic leader balancing ties with the European Union, Russia, China, and Israel. Born in Belgrade in 1970, Vučić entered politics in 1993 with Vojislav Šešelj’s far right Serbian Radical Party (SRS) and drew condemnation for his infamous 1995 parliamentary outburst to kill 100 Muslims for every Serb killed, nine days after the Srebrenica genocide.

In 2008, he left SRS over the party’s support for Serbia’s EU membership and co-founded SNS, a centre to far right party which later emerged as Serbia’s largest party in 2012. Vučić went on to consolidate a dominant-party system while pursuing EU accession, economic liberalisation and dialogue with Kosovo. The SNS ruled Serbia from 2012 to 2026.

Also Read: Brazil nips Latin America’s Trump tide with dramatic win for Lula: ‘Nobody’s backyard’

Will Serbia now be part of EU? The student movement’s programme offers little clarity on its international priorities, while its statements suggest it could maintain the outgoing government’s positions on two contentious issues.

In a May 2026 memorandum, the movement described Kosovo as an “inalienable and integral part of Serbia” and a component of Serbian national identity, advocating a settlement within Serbia’s constitutional framework. In September, it opposed sanctions on Russia, which the outgoing government has also refused to support. Whether these positions would carry over into government remains unclear.

Public opinion among supporters of the student-backed list also suggests an appetite for closer European ties: 75 percent favour stronger relations with the EU, compared with just 10 percent who prefer closer relations with Russia.

Serbia applied for European Union membership in December 2009, received candidate status in March 2012 and formally began accession negotiations in January 2014. Accession progress has remained slow amid EU concerns over the rule of law, press freedom, Serbia’s limited alignment with the bloc’s foreign policy and sanctions against Russia, and the unresolved status of Kosovo.

The Kosovo-Serbia conflict is a political and territorial dispute rooted in ethnic tensions between Albanians and Serbs. The conflict escalated into the 1998–1999 Kosovo War and remains unresolved, with Serbia continuing to refuse recognition of Kosovo’s independence.

EU leaders Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa however welcomed the outcome, voicing hope for a reset in relations with Serbia, despite the student movement’s unclear position on European integration.

The election was also watched internationally as part of 10 pivotal days of voting around the world, in which right-wing forces face off against pro-democracy movements. The student-led victory in Serbia is expected to reverberate across Europe, adding momentum to youth and student protests that have shaken governments across the continent.

I have just spoken by phone with the leaders of the Students' List @studentblokade , who won the elections in Serbia, to congratulate them on their victory. I assured them of Hungary’s support. I was delighted to hear how much strength our victory in April had given them during…

— Magyar Péter (Ne féljetek) (@magyarpeterMP) October 25, 2026

Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar was the first EU national leader to congratulate the victors, comparing their success with his own win over Viktor Orbán earlier this year. “I was delighted to hear how much strength our victory in April had given them during this difficult struggle,” he added on X.

A tragedy that became a national movement In Serbia, what began as weekly student demonstrations after the 2024 tragedy grew into a movement demanding justice on university campuses and city streets and soon spread into communities. Farmers, actors, judges and other groups joined the protests, turning a student campaign into a broader challenge to the government.

In January 2025, Prime Minister Miloš Vučević resigned, saying the move was intended to “defuse tensions”. Two months later, Belgrade witnessed what was described as Serbia’s largest-ever anti-government protest.

As the movement grew, students organised themselves through assemblies, or plenums, rather than relying on a conventional leadership structure. The decentralised approach allowed the campaign to expand while maintaining its identity as a movement driven by students and ordinary citizens rather than established political figures.

By the time Vučić announced snap elections in September, the protesters had begun converting their public momentum into an organised electoral campaign. They staged rallies, visited rural areas that had long been Vučić strongholds and went door-to-door, presenting themselves as anti-establishment candidates. Their slogan was blunt: “Serbia or Mafia?”

Initially, Vučić sought to describe the protesters as “well-intentioned.” Ahead of the election, however, he accused them of trying to “bring down” Serbia. Even after conceding defeat Sunday night, the 56-year-old alleged that the movement had the backing of unnamed “European countries and the American deep state”.

Also Read: France to Italy, cost-of-living protests rock EU: Stores looted, 140-year-old landmark set on fire

What is Student List’s programme? The elected members of parliament will be responsible for delivering what amounts to the movement’s manifesto. The students have said they were looking for people who could enter public institutions and “do their jobs responsibly and not forget why they are there”.

Under an 11-point programme, the student movement wants to eradicate corruption by establishing a police unit to arrest those responsible for it, purge the internal affairs ministry of officials who broke rules while cracking down on protesters or who have links to organised crime, reform Serbia’s media landscape and free the public broadcaster from political control, and end political patronage in public enterprises by stopping the recruitment of party loyalists.

Although the students themselves have not been elected, they are the ones who made promises to the Serbian people. They will, therefore, face pressure to ensure that the parliamentary representatives they selected follow through on the movement’s manifesto.

For his part, Vučić has shown little sign of accepting the movement’s victory as the end of his political struggle. In the speech to party supporters on Sunday evening, he said the students had destroyed two years of life in Serbia and would be defeated “faster by a campaign demanding accountability for a tragedy to a national political force challenging the government itself”.

Who will run Serbia now? The students’ victory has created a new political challenge: identifying who will govern the country. According to reports, it will not be the students themselves, because they did not stand for election. The movement appears to have judged that voters might be reluctant to support a parliamentary list made up of candidates with little life experience.

Although Ilija Srdanović, a cardiology professor in Novi Sad, topped the Student List, he is not widely regarded as the most likely candidate for prime minister. At least 135 people on the list are thought to have won seats in parliament. They include former basketball star Dejan Bodiroga, who was 24th on the list; renowned actor Tihomir Stanić, who was eighth; opera singer Nikola Mikić, who was 46th; and Dejan Šoškić, the former governor of the National Bank of Serbia, who was 27th. The list also includes a substantial number of professors.

Šoškić’s name has been mentioned in connection with the top government post. He has spoken about economic reforms he would pursue and has faced extensive criticism in pro-government media.

The absence of a clearly established leadership could also complicate the transition from protest to government. A movement that drew strength from its decentralised structure will now have to make decisions, negotiate political differences and manage institutions.

The Russia pivot Vučić’s political defeat also carries implications for Serbia’s foreign relationships. He campaigned aggressively through round-the-clock coverage on pro-government media, attacking his opponents as ‘foreign mercenaries’. He contrasted their campaign with his own plans to build prosperity through new roads and hospitals.

In the process, he moved away from the pro-EU positioning that had helped his populist party come to power in 2012, repeatedly boasting of the support of Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Speaking to the state broadcaster RTS during the campaign, Vučić claimed Putin understood that there would be no sanctions against Russia only if the populists won. “It is no coincidence that Vladimir Putin said he hopes that I will be the prime minister.”

His relationship with Moscow has been a prominent feature of his political positioning. In September, Vučić defied the EU by allowing what it describes as a hero’s funeral in Belgrade for Ratko Mladić, the former Bosnian Serb army commander convicted of genocide by a UN court.

Vučić has also enjoyed strong support from China’s President Xi Jinping. The two leaders have described their relationship as an “ironclad friendship.”

Xi has consistently backed Vučić politically, sending high-profile congratulations following his re-election victories and expressing support for Serbia’s national sovereignty. In May, during Vučić’s state visit to Beijing, Xi personally awarded him China’s Friendship Medal, the country’s highest state honour for foreign nationals.

(Edited by Tony Rai)

item.title: アンソロピックが米ＩＰＯ申請書公開、巨額赤字も売上高は急拡大
item.description:
Manya Saini Echo Wang
[２６日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開発の米アンソロピックは２６日、...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アンソロピックが米ＩＰＯ申請書公開、巨額赤字も売上高は急拡大 22:30 配信

１０月１９日撮影　REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

Manya Saini　Echo Wang

[２６日　ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開発の米アンソロピックは２６日、米国での新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）申請書類を公開した。書類では巨額の赤字と急速な売上高の伸びが明らかになり、開発に多額の費用がかかる中でも、世界経済を変革し得るＡＩシステムの構築を目指す姿勢を示した。

目論見書は、過去１年間の同社の急成長を浮き彫りにした。成長を支えたのは大手テクノロジー企業による急激な支出拡大で、ＡＩ関連株の上昇を促す一方、割高な株価評価や債務増加への懸念も招いている。

２０２６年上期の純損失は８０７億ドルと大幅に拡大した。主に、転換社債の公正価値が上昇したことが響いた。同期の売上高は約１６３億ドルだった。

６月３０日までの３カ月間の売上高は、前年同期比１３６８％増と急増した。

アンソロピックのＩＰＯは、競合するオープンＡＩを含め、米金融市場が主要ＡＩ企業をどう評価するかを測る基準になるとみられる。

市場の変動を受けて複数の企業が上場を延期する中でも、アンソロピックは上場計画を進めている。高度なモデルの開発・運用にはコンピューティングインフラへの巨額投資が必要で、ＩＰＯは多額の費用を伴うＡＩ構想の実現に向け、潤沢な資金を調達する機会となる。

＜ＡＩの可能性と危険性の両立＞

今回の申請書類では、業績や成長動向、ＩＰＯ計画など、公開前に内容の一部を伝えたロイターの一連の独自報道が確認された。

ロイターは、アンソロピックが最近の投資家向けイベントで財務情報の一部を開示した後、既存株主や出資を検討する投資家の一部が同社の評価額を約１兆５０００億ドルと見積もっていると報じていた。１週間前の約２兆ドルから低下した。

同社は目論見書で「われわれの成功は、最先端で最も高性能なＡＩモデルを開発し続ける能力に大きく依存しており、それができなければ事業に悪影響が及ぶ可能性がある」と記した。

今回のＩＰＯは、アンソロピック自身の研究が高度なＡＩシステムへの懸念を提起する中で行われる。管理された条件下での試験では、コードの破壊工作や詐欺行為の支援、情報操作といった行動が確認された。

こうした研究結果は、企業が商用化を競う中、ますます強力になるＡＩシステムをどう制御し続けるかという懸念を強めている。

目論見書では、同社のＡＩモデルが「自己保全的な行動」を示す可能性があるとし、「停止に抵抗する」試みや「情報を隠ぺい・操作する」試み、「恐喝に似た」行動などのリスクを挙げた。

アンソロピックはＩＰＯ完了後、ナスダックに銘柄コード「ＡＮＴ」で上場する。売り出す株式数や仮条件の価格帯など、募集条件は明らかにしなかった。

＜売上高が急拡大＞

研究者チームが２０２１年に設立したアンソロピックは、今年５月の資金調達で９６５０億ドルの評価額を付けた。この資金調達には、シリコンバレーや米金融界の有力企業が参加した。

アンソロピックは目論見書で「ＡＩがこれほど豊富に利用できるようになれば、工業化や電力、半導体、インターネットの影響を上回る形で、世界経済のあらゆる分野が急速に変革されると考えている」と記した。計算資源とインフラにかかる費用が金額ベースで増加し、当面は営業費用の中で最大の項目であり続けると見込んでいる。

また、売上高と売掛金が限られた数の顧客や販売経路に集中していると説明した。

アンソロピックは、最先端のＡＩシステム構築を巡り、オープンＡＩと激しい主導権争いを続けている。オープンＡＩは６月に非公開でＩＰＯを申請しており、２０２７年初めまでに上場すると見込まれている。オープンＡＩのサム・アルトマンＣＥＯは９月、ＡＩの安全性への懸念を理由に２６年中は上場しないと述べた。２０３０年までにＡＩが人類を絶滅させるリスクは、たとえ１０％でも「容認できない」とした。

今回のＩＰＯを引き受ける米金融機関の幹事団は、ゴールドマン・サックスとモルガン・スタンレーが主導する。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：トランプ米大統領、任期中の利下げは望み薄　市場は高金利長期化を想定 焦点：トランプ政権の影で歩み寄るカナダとＥＵ、準加盟提示でも見える限界 最終更新: 10/26(月) 23:15 ロイター

item.title: Anthropic's IPO: A close look at AI frontrunner's rapid growth, spiraling costs
item.description: Anthropic unveiled its US initial public offering paperwork on Monday, setting up for a blockbuster market debut that would test investors' willingness to fund the AI juggernaut's bills amid growing worries over the massive debt-fueled spending.
item.dc:creator: Deborah Sophia
item.content:encoded: Anthropic unveiled its US initial public offering paperwork on Monday, setting up for a blockbuster market debut that would test investors' willingness to fund the AI juggernaut's bills amid growing worries over the massive debt-fueled spending. The company had submitted a [USN:L4N4291D9 TEXT:"confidential filing"] in June. In the recent weeks, exclusive reporting from Reuters highlighted its [USN:L6N45L00I TEXT:"sweeping AI ambitions"], [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"mounting costs"] and concerns about the "[USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:"existential risks to humanity"]" that advanced AI poses. Here are a few details on Anthropic's financials, business structure, and where it stands in the global AI race: BACKGROUND AND FINANCES Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic is the startup behind the Claude family of AI models. Across four tiers - Fable, Opus, Sonnet and Haiku - Claude powers products such as Anthropic's chatbot, coding agent and the enterprise-focused Claude Cowork AI agent. Anthropic's early focus on training its models for coding tasks propelled the company to the forefront of the AI race and helped it draw a steady stream of enterprise customers. A majority of its revenue comes from businesses paying for its models per use, measured in "tokens" of information processed, in what Anthropic calls "consumption-based" revenue. It also generates revenue from its paid customer subscription tiers such as "Pro" and "Max". That has helped Anthropic grow its revenue to $4.59 billion in 2025 from $386 million a year ago and $41 million in 2023. For the six months ended June 2026, Anthropic's revenue was $16.29 billion. But the rapid growth is accompanied by bigger losses. Its operating loss for the first half of 2026 was $693 million. In 2025, it was $8.06 billion, up from $2.98 billion a year ago. COSTS, COMPUTE DEMAND AND CIRCULAR AI INVESTMENTS Computing power is Anthropic's biggest expense. The company's costs include computing fees paid to cloud services providers such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, costs tied to data center facilities and renting data center capacity, equipment leases and energy bills. Over the past three years, Anthropic's compute and infrastructure expenses have dwarfed its revenue. The company has committed more than [USN:L1N45K0RM TEXT:"$500 billion"] in spending with six partners over a decade - one of the largest AI buildout commitments on record. Anthropic said many portions of its agreements are non-cancelable or require payments regardless of usage. It has committed to spend at least $110 billion with Amazon (AMZN.O) , about $114.5 billion with Google (GOOGL.O) and $44.9 billion with Microsoft for cloud computing over the next seven to 10 years. But some of those companies are also its largest backers. Amazon and Google are among Anthropic's top shareholders, marking yet another example of the circular financing structures that have dominated capital flows in the AI industry. Amazon has invested at least $13 billion in Anthropic and has agreed to invest up to $20 billion more. Google has committed up to $40 billion to Anthropic. GOVERNANCE AND STRUCTURE Anthropic is a public benefit corporation, or PBC, meaning it is legally obligated to balance profitability goals for investors with developing AI for the benefit of humanity. An independent body elects a majority of its board. The company, helmed by Dario Amodei as CEO and his sister Daniela, as president and chair of the board, will continue to operate as a PBC after its listing. It expects to keep its founders and an independent trust in control, in a structure that could limit investor oversight and public shareholders' influence. The company has said it needs to concentrate control and capital in fewer hands to reduce AI's risks. Under this arrangement, a majority vote of its seven co-founders will direct a single share of Class F stock that amounts to 50.1% of the total voting power over key corporate matters, including the election of some board directors and other matters submitted to investors. COMPETITION Anthropic's most direct competitor is OpenAI, the creator of ChatGPT, whose 2022 launch kick-started the global race to advance and adopt AI technologies. Following Anthropic's lead in the enterprise market, OpenAI has also sharpened its focus on products for developers and business customers. Anthropic is also locked in a race with Elon Musk's SpaceX and Alphabet's Google. All of them are spending billions of dollars into model development, data centers and specialized AI chips as they vie for dominance in generative AI. Ramp data, which captures a slice of AI spending by business customers, showed Anthropic accounted for 60.1% of AI token spending in the week ended October 11. The startup has gained ground against rivals increase spending on AI services.

item.title: S&P Dow Jones partners with Kalshi for index-based events contracts, use prediction data
item.description: S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi on Monday signed a preferred-provider agreement, allowing the prediction market platform to list event contracts linked to prominent benchmarks while S&P will construct new indexes using the partner's data.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: S&P Dow Jones Indices and Kalshi on Monday signed a preferred-provider agreement, allowing the prediction market platform to list event contracts linked to prominent benchmarks while S&P will construct new indexes using the partner's data. Here are more details: The agreement provides a trust cushion for Kalshi, which has battled allegations of being a gambling platform, as S&P DJI is a well-known and trusted name in the financial world Upcoming event contracts on the prediction market will settle against official index values published by S&P DJI, the companies said "S&P DJI is the gold standard for benchmarks. Bringing that standard to Kalshi is an important step toward accelerating retail and institutional demand," Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour said in a statement The partnership will also leverage Kalshi's prediction data to build new S&P indices tracking economics, politics, and sporting events marking the financial information provider's foray into the nascent prediction market world "Our collaboration extends S&P DJI's role as the world's leading benchmark provider into one of the fastest-growing categories in financial markets," said Cathy Clay, CEO of S&P Dow Jones Indices The rapidly expanding prediction market industry, pioneered by platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket, has gained prominence by enabling users to wager on outcomes ranging from sports and elections to military operations

item.title: Las refinerías rusas aumentan la producción de diésel tras el acuerdo con EEUU: fuentes
item.description: Las refinerías rusas están aumentando la producción de diésel en octubre después de que el Gobierno concediera cuotas de exportación a raíz del acuerdo de suministro alcanzado entre el Kremlin y Estados Unidos, según afirmaron dos fuentes del sector cercanas al asunto.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las refinerías rusas están aumentando la producción de diésel en octubre después de que el Gobierno concediera cuotas de exportación a raíz del acuerdo de suministro alcanzado entre el Kremlin y Estados Unidos, según afirmaron dos fuentes del sector cercanas al asunto. El presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, declaró el 9 de octubre que su par ruso, Vladimir Putin, había aceptado un acuerdo para suministrar gasóleo desde Rusia a Estados Unidos y a los mercados mundiales, a cambio de que Washington levantara temporalmente sus sanciones sobre el combustible ruso. Rusia confirmó el acuerdo y Trump señaló que Rusia entregaría más de 300.000 toneladas (unos 2,25 millones de barriles) de diésel de forma inmediata, seguidas de otras 500.000 toneladas en noviembre y 1 millón justo después. Afirmó que Rusia entregaría 3 millones de toneladas más, dependiendo del estado de sus refinerías. Los operadores señalaron que, a partir del 1 de octubre, el Gobierno ruso había concedido excepciones a su actual prohibición de exportación de gasóleo para establecer cuotas que permitieran a Rusia suministrar combustible en el marco del acuerdo con Trump. Desde que entró en vigor la prohibición de exportación de diésel ruso en agosto, sus empresas petroleras han tenido que recortar la producción para satisfacer las necesidades nacionales, al tiempo que limitaban los suministros a los países de Asia Central en virtud de acuerdos intergubernamentales. Fuentes del sector indicaron que la producción de gasóleo rusa descendió en la primera quincena de octubre a unas 160.000 toneladas diarias, frente a las 175.000 toneladas de septiembre. Tras la llegada de las nuevas cuotas de exportación este mes, la producción comenzó a aumentar hasta las 180.000 toneladas diarias. El consumo interno suele descender hasta unas 140.000 toneladas al día en octubre, según las fuentes, que aluden a factores estacionales como la finalización de la cosecha de cereales y la temporada de conducción del verano boreal. Esto dejaría al menos 40.000 toneladas al día, o más de un millón de toneladas al mes, disponibles para la exportación. De esa cantidad, entre 0,2 y 0,3 millones de toneladas podrían ser necesarias para los países vecinos, añadieron las fuentes.

item.title: B3 cita queda de 10% e aciona circuit breaker na abertura do pregão à vista após reeleição de Lula
item.description: A B3 acionou o "circuit breaker" nesta segunda-feira, suspendendo por 30 minutos a negociação dos ativos à vista, renda fixa privada e opções referenciadas em ações, BDR, Ibovespa, Ibovespa B3 BR+, IBrX-50, Índice Small Cap e ETFs.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A B3 (B3SA3.SA) acionou o "circuit breaker" nesta segunda-feira, suspendendo por 30 minutos a negociação dos ativos à vista, renda fixa privada e opções referenciadas em ações, BDR, Ibovespa, Ibovespa B3 BR+, IBrX-50, Índice Small Cap e ETFs. O mecanismo foi acionado após queda de 10% em relação ao fechamento anterior, afirmou a B3, citando que comunicará em breve o horário de reabertura da negociação. Tal reação ocorre após reeleição de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva para a Presidência, que contrariou as expectativas do mercado e trazia preocupações com o cenário fiscal do país. De acordo com agentes financeiros, o mercado havia se posicionado para uma vitória do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno da eleição, principalmente após o filho do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro liderar o primeiro turno. Investidores enxergavam uma mudança em Brasília como uma possibilidade de melhora das contas públicas do país. De acordo com as regras da B3, após um primeiro circuit breaker, se a queda alcançar 15% na volta das operações a negociação é novamente interrompida, então por 1 hora. Na volta, se cair 20%, a B3 pode determinar a suspensão da negociação por um período por ela definido. No mercado futuro, a B3 ampliou duas vezes os limites inferiores de oscilação diária para os contratos do Ibovespa - de 10% para 15% antes da abertura e após o início dos negócios elevou novamente o piso para 20%, em decisão que também inclui os mini contratos futuros do índice. Por volta de 10h10, o contrato com vencimento em 16 de dezembro afundava 16,74%, a 173.260 pontos.

item.title: Chilena Codelco y BHP firman acuerdo para iniciar exploración de proyecto Anillo en norte de Chile
item.description: La estatal chilena Codelco, una de las mayores productoras mundiales de cobre, anunció el lunes que firmó un acuerdo con la minera global BHP para la exploración de su pertenencia minera Anillo, ubicada en la región de Antofagasta en el norte de Chile.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La estatal chilena Codelco, una de las mayores productoras mundiales de cobre, anunció el lunes que firmó un acuerdo con la minera global BHP para la exploración de su pertenencia minera Anillo, ubicada en la región de Antofagasta en el norte de Chile. BHP podrá invertir hasta 40 millones de dólares para explorar y estudiar el potencial minero de las pertenencias. La firma del contrato se concretó la semana pasada durante la London Metal Exchange Week 2026, dijo un comunicado de la estatal, luego de completarse las autorizaciones legales para la constitución de derechos sobre pertenencias mineras de Codelco que no forman parte de yacimientos en actual explotación. El acuerdo para exploración se había anunciado el año pasado.

item.title: From Amazon to Google, the deep-pocketed investors in Anthropic
item.description: Only a few startups have attracted as much investor conviction as Anthropic. Backed by some of the biggest names in technology and finance, the AI company has seen its valuation soar through successive funding rounds.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Only a few startups have attracted as much investor conviction as Anthropic. Backed by some of the biggest names in technology and finance, the AI company has seen its valuation soar through successive funding rounds. Its [USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"initial public offering"] now offers a closely watched test of whether investors beyond Silicon Valley share that enthusiasm for the leaders of the AI boom. Here's a look at the key investors backing the Claude maker: Investor Details Amazon Amazon has invested at least $13 billion in Anthropic and in April agreed to invest up to an additional $20 billion. Anthropic also committed to spend more than $100 billion on the e-commerce giant's cloud services over 10 years Alphabet's Google Google has committed up to $40 billion to Anthropic, including an initial $10 billion investment announced in April. The partnership provides Anthropic with cloud infrastructure and access to Google's AI chips, which are used to train and run Claude models Spark Capital Spark Capital led Anthropic's $450 million Series C round in May 2023 and gained board representation through general partner Yasmin Razavi Lightspeed Venture Partners Lightspeed led the $3.5 billion Series E round in March 2025 and later co-led the $13 billion Series F round at a $183 billion valuation in September that year Fidelity Management & Research Fidelity participated in Series E and co-led the $13 billion Series F financing at a $183 billion valuation. The firm's other investments include Databricks and CoreWeave Salesforce Ventures Salesforce Ventures participated in the $450 million Series C round and the $3.5 billion Series E financing. The software firm's venture arm has also invested in firms such as Cohere and Chainguard ICONIQ Capital ICONIQ led the $13 billion Series F round at a $183 billion valuation and later co-led the $30 billion Series G financing. The venture capital firm's investments include OpenAI and smart ring maker Oura GIC Singapore's sovereign wealth fund led the $30 billion Series G round at a $380 billion valuation. GIC has also invested in AI voice generation startup ElevenLabs Coatue Management Coatue led the $30 billion Series G financing and later co-led the $65 billion Series H round. The investment firm has also financed companies such as Canva and CoreWeave D1 Capital Partners D1 Capital invested across multiple large financings including Series E, Series F, Series G and Series H. The firm has holdings in Cognition AI and SpaceX Sequoia Capital Sequoia was a significant investor in Series G and became one of the lead investors in the $65 billion Series H round at a $965 billion valuation Altimeter Capital Altimeter invested in the September 2025 $13 billion fundraise and was a lead investor in the $65 billion Series H financing at a $965 billion valuation Jaan Tallinn Skype co-founder Tallinn led Anthropic's first institutional financing, a $124 million Series A round in 2021. The angel investor has also funded open-source AI startup Zyphra and Rain AI Eric Schmidt The former Google chief executive has backed Anthropic personally and is among the company's best-known individual investors. Schmidt has also funded Yann LeCun's Advanced Machine Intelligence Menlo Ventures Menlo participated in major late-stage financings, including the $3.5 billion Series E round at a $61.5 billion valuation

Australia give Smith chance to prove fitness ahead of decider

CAPE TOWN, Oct 26 : Australia will give key batter Steve Smith as much time as possible to prove his fitness ahead of the third and final test against South Africa at Newlands, captain Pat Cummins said on Monday. Smith injured his neck in South Africa’s innings and 31-run victory in the second test in Gqeberha which levelled the series at 1-1 going into the decider in Cape Town starting on Tuesday. "Hopefully, it all goes well and he'll be there," Cummins told reporters on Monday. "But we just want to wait for that last piece of the puzzle (before naming a team). Cummins said Cameron Green would bat “preferably in the middle order”, which will likely mean Matt Renshaw opening with Travis Head after Nic Maddinson was dropped from the squad.

For Smith, it would be a return to the scene of his darkest day after his role as captain in the "Sandpapergate" scandal that rocked Australian cricket in 2018. “He's been awesome this tour," Cummins said. “In the last couple of years, probably particularly the last 12 months, it feels like he's in a really good place and he's enjoying his cricket. “He’s getting himself out (and about), whether it is playing golf or going for coffee club every morning. He's been super invested in what's going on and very helpful for me out in the middle." Smith has averaged a little over 20 in four innings with the bat and took a blow to the head in the first test, before injuring his neck in the second. “He looks in total control of how he's going about his work. He's one of the greatest batters we've ever had. You don't play 100 odd tests without matches where you're not 100 per cent fit," Cummins said. Cummins was part of the side involved in the Sandpapergate scandal, though denies any knowledge of events, and another infamous test Australia played in Cape Town in 2011. "My first ever test experience was here. I was running the drinks and we got bowled out for 47. So that was a wild introduction," he said with a smile.

Source: Reuters

item.title: ヨルダン教会襲撃で3人逮捕、他の組織との関連確認されず
item.description:
AbdelHadi Ramahi Eman Abouhassira Nayera Abdallah
[アル・ジュダイダ（ヨルダン）／ドバイ ２６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
AbdelHadi Ramahi　Eman Abouhassira　Nayera Abdallah

[アル・ジュダイダ（ヨルダン）／ドバイ ２６日 ロイター] - ヨルダンの治安当局は２６日、９人が死亡した教会襲撃事件に関与した疑いで、銃撃戦の末に兄弟２人と義理の兄弟１人を逮捕した。政府高官が明らかにした。容疑者らと他の組織とのつながりはないとみられ、独自に行動したとの見方を示した。

この事件は２３日、首都アンマンの南西約１２０キロにあるカラク県ハムード村のギリシャ正教会で葬儀中に発生し、ほかにも４０人が負傷した。目撃者によると、銃撃は数分間続いたという。

公安当局はカラクの廃屋に潜伏していた容疑者を発見したと説明。投降を拒否して治安部隊を攻撃したため、部隊が応戦し、３人全員を負傷させた上で逮捕した。

治安部隊側に負傷者はでなかった。容疑者らが所持していた複数の銃器や弾薬が見つかったという。

ファラヤ内相と公安総局のアブドラ・マアイタ少将は記者会見で、過激派によるテロを容認しないと表明。ファラヤ氏は「事件はまだ解決しておらず、捜査は続いている。現時点で、彼らと他の組織とのつながりを示すものはない」と述べた。

容疑者の氏名を公表せず、イスラム過激派組織との関係の有無についても明らかにしなかった。

中東で比較的安定しているヨルダンでは、こうした暴力事件は極めて異例だ。

item.title: Egypt approves military support for Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks escalate
item.description: The move could push Cairo directly into the regional conflict that has expanded with intensified attacks by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis on the Gulf kingdom.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Parliament authorised Egypt's military on Monday to provide support to help defend Saudi Arabia, parliamentarians said and local media reported, a move that could push Cairo directly into the regional conflict that has expanded with intensified attacks by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis on the Gulf kingdom. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi had [USN:L6N46403J TEXT:"asked parliament"] last week to approve defending its Gulf Arab ally and the world's biggest oil exporter if Riyadh requests help against the Houthis, whose advances also threaten the strategic [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb Strait"] — a gateway to Egypt's Suez Canal. Egypt has frequently condemned Iranian and Iranian-backed attacks on Gulf countries but has not publicly engaged in direct combat or joined the Mecca [USN:L1N45R0S7 TEXT:"mutual defence"] pact between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey that was [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"signed in August"]. Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said this month that Egyptian membership in the pact remains "under serious consideration." Egypt, the Arab world's most populous state with one of the region's largest militaries, joined the Saudi-led coalition in an earlier phase of Yemen's war in March 2015 mainly as a naval partner, sending warships to secure Red Sea shipping lanes while pledging air support. It also deployed around 800 ground troops but played only a limited combat role. Egypt was involved in a costly military intervention in Yemen in the 1960s and has not undertaken a large-scale foreign ground deployment since the 1991 Gulf War. Saudi Arabia is a major political and financial partner of Cairo, providing billions of dollars in aid, deposits at the central bank and energy supplies under Sisi. Fighting between the Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government and the Houthi militia, which controls the capital Sanaa, has escalated in recent weeks, becoming a volatile front in the US-Israeli war on Iran . The Houthis have attacked [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"Riyadh's international airport"] and the state oil giant [USN:L1N45Z0HH TEXT:"Saudi Aramco"], disrupting flights and oil exports, while aid agencies have warned of worsening conditions in Yemen, already suffering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. Abdelatty and Egyptian intelligence chief Hassan Rashad travelled to Riyadh on Wednesday to deliver a letter to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman from Sisi, who said Egypt's support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders rather than attacking Yemen. Abdelatty said after that visit that Cairo advocates exploring [USN:L1N4680Z9 TEXT:""every opportunity""] to resolve the Yemen conflict diplomatically. The Saudi crown prince [USN:S8N452004 TEXT:"visited Sisi in Cairo"] on September 15 to discuss security and navigation in the Red Sea after the fighting in Yemen reignited.

item.title: Taxas dos DIs de longo prazo sobem mais de 260 pontos-base após vitória de Lula
item.description: As taxas dos DIs dispararam nesta manhã de segunda-feira após o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) vencer o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, surpreendendo o mercado.
item.dc:creator: Fabricio Castro
item.content:encoded: As taxas dos DIs dispararam nesta manhã de segunda-feira após o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) vencer o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, surpreendendo o mercado. Às 9h58, a taxa do DI (Depósito Interfinanceiro) para janeiro de 2028 estava em 14,915%, em alta de 206 pontos-base ante o ajuste de 12,859% da sessão anterior. Na ponta longa da curva a termo, a taxa do DI para janeiro de 2035 estava em 15,375%, com elevação de 263 pontos-base ante 12,745%. Lula venceu a disputa pelo Planalto com 51,79% dos votos válidos, contra 48,21% do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Como o mercado estava em grande parte posicionado para uma vitória de Flávio, o ajuste nesta manhã é intenso. Na noite de domingo, profissionais consultados pela Reuters já haviam [USN:L2N46C034 TEXT:"projetado"] um forte avanço das taxas dos DIs, em especial nos contratos com prazos mais longos, que refletem mais diretamente a perspectiva para a política fiscal. No dia seguinte ao primeiro turno, quando Flávio ficou à frente de Lula, a taxa do DI para janeiro de 2035 chegou a ceder mais de 130 pontos-base, em meio à euforia do mercado com a possibilidade de o senador vencer a disputa. Por trás da euforia estava a leitura de que, com Flávio no Planalto, cresceriam as chances de um ajuste nas contas públicas. Como Lula venceu o segundo turno, garantindo mais um mandato, a curva a termo brasileira está enfrentando um forte ajuste de alta nesta segunda-feira. Em função das oscilações, a B3 elevou, por meio de comunicado, todos os limites de alta das taxas dos DIs, em todos os vencimentos. Em outra medida, o Tesouro Nacional informou nesta manhã o [USN:S0N45S019 TEXT:"cancelamento"] do tradicional leilão de títulos indexados à inflação na terça-feira e o cancelamento do leilão de papéis prefixados na quinta-feira. Por outro lado, o Tesouro manteve o leilão de Letras Financeiras do Tesouro (LFTs), títulos indexados à taxa básica Selic, previsto para terça-feira. Ao anunciar os cancelamentos, o Tesouro busca não estimular taxas ainda mais elevadas nos mercados de títulos e de DIs. item.title: Surgery Partners to be taken private by Bon Secours affiliate in $5.7 billion deal
item.description: Surgery Partners said on Monday it would be taken private by HealthSpan Partners, an affiliate of nonprofit hospital system Bon Secours Mercy Health, in a deal valued at about $5.7 billion including debt, sending its shares up 46%.
item.dc:creator: Christy Santhosh
item.content:encoded: Surgery Partners (SGRY.O) said on Monday it would be taken private by HealthSpan Partners, an affiliate of nonprofit hospital system Bon Secours Mercy Health, in a deal valued at about $5.7 billion including debt, sending its shares up 46%. Private equity group Bain Capital, which has been a minority shareholder since 2017 and owns 39% of Surgery Partners, will back the deal and retain a major ownership stake after closing, the companies said. The remaining shareholders will receive $23.50 per share, implying a premium of 49% to the stock's last close. The deal, expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, highlights a growing push into outpatient surgery by healthcare operators, with not-for-profit health system Ascension having purchased surgical firm AmSurg for $3.9 billion earlier this year. The addition of Surgery Partners will expand Bon Secours Mercy Health's US footprint well beyond its more than 45 hospitals, according to the hospital system, adding over 200 sites across 30 states and about 5,000 affiliated physicians. The deal also ends a two-year strategic review during which Surgery Partners drew interest from potential buyers including Bain Capital, [USN:L4N3SK0YE TEXT:"whose bid to"] take the company private last year was rebuffed. Surgery Partners operates outpatient surgery centers, short-stay hospitals and related healthcare services across the US. "From a strategic perspective, there is some market overlap in Ohio and Kentucky, but the potential transaction would substantially broaden the system's (Bon Secours Mercy Health) national footprint, so we do not expect meaningful FTC antitrust risk issues," said Mizuho analyst Ann Hynes. Hynes said Bain retaining its ownership position under the proposed transaction is expected to help the deal close. In 2025, Surgery Partners generated $3.31 billion in revenue and reported an adjusted profit of 47 cents per share.

item.title: Netanyahu touts Trump endorsement on eve of vote, suggests they may restart war on Iran
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boasted of his endorsement from Donald Trump on the eve of Israel's election, suggesting the two leaders could restart their war against Iran if he wins, after Trump said they should "finish the job".
item.dc:creator: Steven Scheer, Emily Rose
item.content:encoded: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu boasted of his endorsement from Donald Trump on the eve of Israel's election, suggesting the two leaders could restart their war against Iran if he wins, after Trump said they should "finish the job". "US President Donald Trump has come with a friendship that has never existed before between an Israeli prime minister and an American president. And it is doubtful we will ever have such a friendly president again," Netanyahu said in a televised appearance late on Sunday night. "He has another two years, and he says he is calling on you to vote for me." In his own social media post on Sunday, Trump, who launched the Iran war jointly with Netanyahu in February, said: "Vote for Bibi Netanyahu for Prime Minister, we have to finish the job that we started!" Netanyahu said Trump was willing to take action "that would finally, finally, remove the Iranian threat", but only as long as Netanyahu himself remains in power. "And I have already instructed the Mossad and the IDF (military) to bring down this regime, to bring down this regime because that is the only way to put an end to this threat," Netanyahu said, referring to Israel's main intelligence service and military. Asked for comment on Netanyahu's remarks, White House Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly said: “As President Trump stated, Iran is in very bad condition, both economically and militarily, and the blockade will remain in full force and effect, with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait." "The United States will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"]," Kelly added via email, referring to the November 3 vote in the US. Netanyahu's leading opponent, centrist former military Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, posted his own comments on social media, praising Trump as "a true friend of Israel". "I value his efforts and his commitment to Israel’s security, and I am confident that he will work in full cooperation with any leader chosen by the people." EISENKOT ACCUSES NETANYAHU OF FEAR-MONGERING Tuesday's vote, Israel's first since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, is the first chance for voters to deliver a [USN:L8N4680E4 TEXT:"verdict on the worst security failure"] in generations and the wars on multiple fronts that followed. With Netanyahu already at the helm of the most right-wing government in Israeli history, politics have shifted even further to the right. Nearly all Jewish-led parties, including that of the hawkish Eisenkot, now [USN:L6N4660BW TEXT:"oppose the "two-state solution" that underpinned decades of peace negotiations"] with the Palestinians. But many voters say the divisive politics of Israel's longest-serving leader make the country weaker. Polls suggest Netanyahu's Likud Party will lose seats, potentially depriving his coalition of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties of its narrow majority. Eisenkot and an array of opposition parties ranging from the rump of the centre-left to the right, also have no clear path to unseat him. Netanyahu, 77, is an unrivaled master of political survival: the only time since 2009 that opponents managed to wrest him briefly from the premiership, it took four inconclusive elections within two years to get him out. He was back 18 months later. Neither side planned major public events for Monday. But both posted on social media, drumming on the election's major themes — for Netanyahu, that he is the only leader with the mettle to face down Israel's enemies; for his opponents, that his divisive politics have weakened the country. Netanyahu shared an AI-generated video on Monday of Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, whose father Ali Khamenei was killed on the first night of US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February. Lying in a hospital bed, the younger Khamenei says his own vote would be "definitely not Bibi. Another term like this and I will be meeting my father sooner than expected." On Sunday Netanyahu posted a computer-generated photo of a mushroom cloud over Tel Aviv, saying Israel was in existential danger from Iran. [USN:L6N46303T TEXT:"Eisenkot responded"] by accusing him of "relying on a campaign of fear-mongering, lies, and threats—including images of nuclear bombs in the heart of Tel Aviv. This time, it won’t work for him." Trump's endorsement of Netanyahu carries its own political risks a week before a legislative election in which his own Republicans are seeking to hold onto power. The Iran war is deeply unpopular in the United States, blamed for a surge in prices especially for fuel. Major fighting has been suspended for months after ceasefire negotiations held without Israeli participation.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO filing shows explosive growth, risks and staggering costs
item.description: Anthropic disclosed steep losses and red-hot revenue growth in its US IPO filing on Monday, as the Claude-parent laid out its ambition to build AI systems capable of reshaping the global economy despite the high costs of developing the technology.
item.dc:creator: Manya Saini, Echo Wang
item.content:encoded: Anthropic disclosed steep losses and red-hot revenue growth in its US IPO filing on Monday, as the Claude-parent laid out its ambition to build AI systems capable of reshaping the global economy despite the high costs of developing the technology. The prospectus highlights [USN:L4N4691FD TEXT:"the AI company's rapid growth"] over the past year, fueled by Big Tech's breakneck spending that has driven a rally in AI stocks while raising concerns about lofty valuations and rising debt. The company also flagged growing risks from AI technology, underscoring concerns over its potential to cause harm which had led CEO Dario Amodei to call for a slowdown in development of advanced models. Anthropic's net loss in the first half of 2026 [USN:L4N4661JI TEXT:"widened sharply"] to $80.7 billion, largely due to a rise in the fair value of bonds convertible into company's shares. Revenue in this period stood at about $16.3 billion. The company's revenue grew a staggering 1,368% in the three months ended June 30 from a year ago, but warned in the prospectus that revenue growth rate could decline over time and fluctuate from time to time. The IPO, which is likely to be as early as later this month, is expected to establish Anthropic, the AI lab behind the viral Claude models, as a benchmark for how Wall Street values leading AI companies, including rival OpenAI. [USN:L6N46811V TEXT:"The IPO push comes"] despite a once-busy fall listing calendar thinning out as choppy markets prompt companies to delay their offerings. Analysts [USN:L6N46C0UF TEXT:"said"] that would give Anthropic access to a deep pool of capital to fund its costly AI ambitions. [USN:L6N4611C1 TEXT:"Growing investor uneasy"] with the debt-fueled AI investment boom has led to a global selloff in AI and tech stocks as they start to doubt if the trillions spent on data centers, chips and computing capacity will generate fast returns to support lofty valuations. Higher borrowing costs and rising bond yields have added to their caution. However, tech companies are still hungry for cash. Meta [USN:L3N46C0RT TEXT:"is aiming"] to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising, while SpaceX has [USN:L6N46C0RJ TEXT:"inked"] a $40 billion deal with Apollo to lease AI chips and server hardware. VALUATION EXPECTATIONS Some current and prospective investors [USN:L6N4611F6 TEXT:"are valuing Anthropic"] at about $1.5 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion a week ago, after the AI startup disclosed some financial details at a [USN:L6N4601DE TEXT:"recent investor event"], Reuters reported. "While Anthropic is well-capitalized, an IPO would give the company some valuable financial flexibility. No company wants to spend too long on the cusp of going public, since that can be a distraction," said Matt Kennedy, senior strategist at Renaissance Capital, a provider of IPO-focused research and ETFs "Maybe they could have gotten a higher valuation next year, but they've decided to "rip the band-aid off". The filing [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"confirmed a series of Reuters "][USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"exclusives"] that offered an early peek at its contents before Anthropic made it public, including details of its financial performance, growth trajectory and IPO plans. BALANCING AI'S PROMISES AND PERILS Anthropic said more than half of Fortune 500 companies and over 30% of Global 2000 firms were customers generating at least $100,000 each in revenue for the company over the 12 months ended September 30. The IPO comes as Anthropic's own research raises concerns about advanced AI systems, which in controlled tests have shown behaviors including code sabotage, fraud assistance and information manipulation. The findings have fueled concerns about how companies can keep powerful AI systems under control as they race to deploy them commercially. The prospectus also [USN:L4N45K1J5 TEXT:"highlighted risks"] associated with its AI models, which it said could exhibit "self-preserving behaviors", including behavior "resembling blackmail". "Our increasing use of AI systems to accelerate our own research and development may cause the capabilities of our models to advance more rapidly than our ability to develop, validate, and implement corresponding safety, alignment, and security measures," it said. The company said it relies on a limited number of cloud services providers such as Amazon, Google and Microsoft and suppliers such as Broadcom for compute and critical parts of its infrastructure These relationships can create "dependencies and potential vulnerabilities", it said. Anthropic will trade on the Nasdaq after the [USN:L4N469189 TEXT:"IPO closes"] under the ticker symbol "ANT". The filing [USN:L4N41X0QE TEXT:"did not reveal"] the terms of its offering, including the number of shares it plans to sell and the proposed price range. RED HOT GROWTH Anthropic, founded in 2021 by a team of researchers, was [USN:L4N4251UW TEXT:"valued at $965 billion"] in May in a funding round that drew some of the biggest names in Silicon Valley and Wall Street. Amazon and Google were among Anthropic's early strategic partners, investing billions of dollars in the startup while providing the cloud infrastructure needed to train and deploy Claude models. "We believe this abundance of AI will rapidly transform every sector of the global economy in ways greater than the impact of industrialization, electricity, semiconductors and the internet," the prospectus said. The company said it expects compute and infrastructure expenses to increase in absolute dollars and remain its largest operating expense for the foreseeable future. Anthropic remains locked in a fierce battle with OpenAI to lead the race to build the most advanced AI systems. The ChatGPT maker confidentially filed for an IPO in June and is expected to list by early 2027. Anthropic's IPO follows that of Elon Musk's SpaceX, which rewrote the IPO record books in June, when it [USN:L6N42G18Z TEXT:"priced"] a $75 billion offering that valued the company at $1.75 trillion. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley were named as the lead banks for the IPO alongside 20 others as underwriters. Morgan Stanley will act as a stabilization agent, overseeing the stock's early trading. The roles mark another major win for Goldman and Morgan Stanley as they had led SpaceX's IPO too.

item.title: Ukraine has waited nearly a month for US to sign off on Patriot missiles, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Ukraine has been waiting for almost a month for the US defence secretary to sign off on critical missile supplies, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine has been waiting for almost a month for the US defence secretary to sign off on critical missile supplies, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure. "In particular, we have been waiting for nearly a month for Mr Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS. I instructed our team to raise this with the American side once again," Zelenskiy said on X. The Ukrainian leader has repeatedly called on the US, which supplies missiles purchased by NATO allies under a program known as PURL, to speed up deliveries ahead of winter. Last week, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged that a batch of interceptors may not have been delivered, but said that the delay was not for political reasons. Delayed missile deliveries are adding to Ukraine's tensions with the US after President Donald Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia and criticised Zelenskiy for Ukraine's unwillingness to stop attacks on Russian refineries. In recent weeks, Ukraine said that at some point it experienced gaps in getting intelligence from the US on Russian missile attacks. It also reported that [USN:L2N46A00O TEXT:"Starlink's military version"] has been throttled for days, disrupting military operations and air defences. Reuters has reported that the [USN:L1N4610ZC TEXT:"order to throttle"] Starshield came from inside the White House. Both SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and US officials have said publicly that any decisions on Starlink and Starshield limitations could only have been taken by the other.

Cadence unveils Nvidia-backed AI models that chipmakers can run in-house

FAST

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 26 : Cadence Design Systems on Monday launched a portfolio of AI models tuned to help design computer chips, deepening its partnership with Nvidia and diverging from rival Synopsys's recent deal with OpenAI. Both companies make software used to design computing chips — a process that involves arranging billions of transistors precisely to meet cost and performance targets — and are racing to have AI "agents" use those tools on behalf of human engineers to speed up the process. The new suite, called Cadence Maestro, introduced on Monday, was built in part on Nvidia's open-weight Nemotron model and secured with Nvidia's OpenShell safety technology, the companies said. Cadence said customers can run the models on its own cloud or any public cloud, or keep them entirely in-house behind their own firewalls and data centers.

They can also fine-tune the models on their own chip designs, and early results show up to 30 per cent higher quality and up to five times better cost-efficiency versus general-purpose models, it added. The Cadence approach contrasts with that of its largest competitor, Synopsys, which on September 30 said it would develop an AI model with OpenAI and share revenue with the ChatGPT maker. That model, GPT-Synopsys, will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure. Paul Cunningham, a Cadence senior vice president, framed Maestro as model-agnostic, noting "there are more (AI) model providers out there than there are (chip design software) vendors." When asked whether Cadence might strike its own deals with proprietary AI labs, Cunningham said both open- and closed-weight approaches are being "pursued equally," and that working with commercial labs is "part of the Maestro vision," though he declined to elaborate. The first Maestro models reach select early-access customers in the fourth quarter, Cadence said.

item.title: T-Mobile debuts wireless plans with customizable perks from streaming to food delivery
item.description: T-Mobile on Monday unveiled wireless plans that let customers pick and swap perks from Netflix to DoorDash, moving away from its traditional strategy of locking benefits into fixed plan tiers.
item.dc:creator: Harshita Varghese
item.content:encoded: T-Mobile (TMUS.O) on Monday unveiled wireless plans that let customers pick and swap perks from Netflix to DoorDash, moving away from its traditional strategy of locking benefits into fixed plan tiers. The move mirrors customizable offerings from rivals such as Verizon, but T-Mobile's new plans include selected streaming, music and other subscriptions at no extra cost beyond the monthly plan price. T-Mobile is betting that offering greater control over benefits will attract customers spending on multiple subscriptions, as competition among US carriers moves beyond network coverage and smartphone promotions Netflix was the most popular benefit in a pilot launched in early October, T-Mobile Chief Marketing Officer Allan Samson told Reuters in an interview Music subscriptions and artificial intelligence services also drew interest, while Xbox gaming was popular among younger customers, he added The new T-Mix plans will be available from next month in three tiers. The Standard tier is priced from $55 for one line, while More starts at $75 and Loaded at $95 The number of perks available will depend on the tier and the number of lines required Partnerships include Apple, DoorDash, Google, Hulu, Netflix, Paramount+, SiriusXM, Xbox and YouTube Customers can also select benefits including Delta SkyMiles, ESPN Unlimited, Google Gemini and device promotions Customers will be able to change selected perks every three months, or during an annual change window. Certain wireless benefits, such as satellite connectivity, can be changed at any time

item.content:encoded: O Tesouro Nacional cancelou nesta segunda-feira os leilões de títulos prefixados e atrelados à inflação previstos para a terça e a quinta-feira, ao mesmo tempo que manteve o leilão de papeis vinculados à taxa básica de juros Selic agendado para a terça-feira, informou o Tesouro em comunicado. "O Tesouro Nacional continuará monitorando as condições de mercado e atuará de forma a assegurar o bom funcionamento do mercado de títulos públicos e de outros ativos relacionados", informou o Tesouro em comunicado. O cancelamento dos leilões acontece em meio a uma forte alta dos juros futuros e a uma expressiva queda dos ativos brasileiros nesta segunda-feira, um dia após a reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, realizado no domingo.

BRUSSELS, Oct 26 : The European Commission said on Monday it had accepted Chinese online retail platform Temu's action plan to remedy a breach of the EU's Digital Services Act, following a fine imposed on the company in May. The plan focuses on five measures to remedy the breach, and Temu now has four months to conduct an interim risk assessment, the Commission, which acts as EU regulator, said in a statement. The Commission had imposed a €200 million ($224.08 million) fine on Temu in May for not doing enough to stop the sale of illegal products. A spokesperson for Temu, which is owned by PDD Holdings, said it welcomed the Commission's approval of its plan under which the company will have to assess possible shortcomings of its content moderation system, among other steps. Temu, along with Shein and other ecommerce platforms, has been hit by the EU imposing €3 fees on low-value ecommerce packages since the start of July. Parcels worth less than €150 previously entered the bloc duty-free. ($1 = 0.8925 euros)

item.title: Apollo deepens Abu Dhabi ties with investment in Mubadala Capital
item.description: Apollo Global Management will acquire a minority stake in Mubadala Capital and commit capital across its investment strategies, the alternative asset management subsidiary of Abu Dhabi wealth fund Mubadala said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: Apollo Global Management (APO.N) will acquire a minority stake in Mubadala Capital and commit capital across its investment strategies, the alternative asset management subsidiary of Abu Dhabi wealth fund Mubadala said on Monday. The US investment group is expected to commit an aggregate $5 billion to Mubadala Capital’s investment strategies together with other strategic investors, which will join as minority shareholders, Mubadala Capital said in a statement. The deal deepens its ties with Mubadala. Apollo will acquire a stake of nearly 10% in the subsidiary, a person familiar with the matter said. Apollo declined to comment on the size of the stake. "Apollo’s investment will help the firm broaden its investor base, expand its strategies, and pursue new opportunities globally," Mubadala Capital said. It added that it will continue to operate independently and will maintain its own governance structure once the deal is completed. In recent years, global investment companies have boosted their presence and ties with the Gulf region, attracted by proximity to some of the world's largest sovereign wealth funds. Wealth funds in Abu Dhabi alone together manage an estimated $1.8 trillion. Mubadala, which had assets under management of $385 billion at the end of last year, is among funds that have been increasing exposure to alternative investments. Last year, Mubadala Capital entered into a $1 billion strategic partnership with New York-based investment firm Fortress to invest in private credit, following previous partnerships with Goldman Sachs and Apollo. "Mubadala has been a trusted partner in seeding and scaling a number of our strategies over the years. This investment in the differentiated asset management platform they have built in Mubadala Capital builds on our existing partnership and reflects our conviction in their business," John Zito, co-president of Apollo Asset Management, said in the statement. Goldman Sachs and Jefferies advised Mubadala Capital, while Morgan Stanley acted as financial advisor to Apollo for the deal, which is expected to close in the fourth quarter.

item.title: Oleshky: the occupied Ukrainian town for which Melania Trump helped broker a ceasefire
item.description: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a localised ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine, an arrangement that will enable aid deliveries and allow evacuations from a frontline town suffering acute shortages of food and medicine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a localised ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine, an arrangement that will enable aid deliveries and allow evacuations from a frontline town suffering acute shortages of food and medicine. The [USN:L1N46911P TEXT:"agreement"] was announced on October 23 and brokered by US first lady Melania Trump, with the additional involvement of Pope Leo, as Washington seeks to revive broader peace talks between Moscow and Kyiv. WHY ARE RESIDENTS OF OLESHKY AT RISK? Oleshky lies on the eastern bank of the Dnipro River in Ukraine's southern Kherson region, opposite Kherson city, which is held by Ukrainian forces. Russian troops seized Oleshky during the first days of their February 2022 invasion and have controlled it ever since. Oleshky has suffered extensive war damage and was hit hard by flooding after the destruction of the nearby Kakhovka dam in 2023. The United States has said only a few thousand people remain in Oleshky, from a prewar population of 24,000. Residents and officials have reported [USN:L8N45K1N1 TEXT:"severe shortages of food"], medicine and other basic supplies. WHAT DOES THE CEASEFIRE INVOLVE? According to Ukrainian and Russian officials, the arrangement provides for a local halt in fighting, the delivery of humanitarian assistance and the evacuation of civilians who wish to leave the town. The two sides said humanitarian corridors would be established to allow aid deliveries and the movement of residents. WHO BROKERED THE DEAL? The White House said Melania Trump helped secure the agreement after becoming involved in discussions on the humanitarian situation in Oleshky. The White House said the first lady and a representative worked with Russian and Ukrainian officials to agree the terms of the ceasefire. Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets publicly thanked Melania Trump and her team for helping coordinate the talks. Russian officials also confirmed the agreement. [USN:L8N4651KU TEXT:"Pope Leo"] also played a role. He held a phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, the Vatican said, and urged Ukraine and Russia to cooperate to let aid and food in. WHAT MIGHT HAPPEN NEXT? The ceasefire is limited in scope and does not address the wider conflict, now in its fifth year. But it is a rare example of direct cooperation between the two sides since the start of the invasion. The Kremlin said on Monday that the truce might serve as a precedent for similar localised ceasefires in the future.

The govt wants to save €900 mn a year by 2027, rising to €3.5 billion from 2035. The cabinet will also present plans for deploying AI to work more productively early next year.

Patrick Van Oosterom

The Dutch Parliament building beside the Hofvijver pond in The Hague, Netherlands, on Thursday, March 18, 2021. Caretaker prime minister Mark Ruttes center-right party, the VVD, won 36 seats in the 150-strong parliament, with the pro-European group D66 in second place with 24 seats, according to a projection early Thursday by Dutch news agency ANP with 63% of votes counted.

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

The Dutch government aims to cut 25,000 civil servant jobs in an AI-led efficiency drive targeting annual savings of €3.5 billion ($3.9 billion).

The central government wants to save €900 million a year by 2027, rising to €3.5 billion from 2035. That amounts to around 25,000 jobs, spread over several years, according to a government statement on Monday. The cabinet will present plans for deploying artificial intelligence to work more productively early next year.

“We cannot keep doing what we have been doing,” State Secretary for Effective Government Eric van den Burg said. “That is why we are going to make tough choices for a central government that really works: simpler, smarter, and smaller.”

Show Full Article

The number of government officials surged to a record 160,000 at the end of 2025, up 41% compared to 2018, despite pledges by previous cabinets to scale back headcount.

The Dutch government budget deficit of 1.8% is one of the smallest in the European Union. Yet the figure and its long-term outlook still raise concerns in the Netherlands, which has a reputation for being fiscally conservative.

item.title: SpaceX enters $40 billion deal with Apollo for AI chip financing
item.description: SpaceX said on Monday an affiliate of Apollo Global Management will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: SpaceX (SPCX.O) said on Monday an affiliate of Apollo Global Management (APO.N) will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion. Each lease will run a little over five years from the day the equipment arrives, according to a regulatory filing. The deal highlights SpaceX's heavy spending, as it tries to capitalize on surging demand for computing power to help bankroll its Moon and Mars ambitions. The company aims to finalize the deal by the end of the year. The leases are expected to start in the first half of 2027, once the chips are delivered. On Sunday, CEO Elon Musk said on X that SpaceX had [USN:L6N46B085 TEXT:""closed" $40 billion"] in debt financing for graphics processing units. Musk said the funding mainly targeted chips arriving in the first and second quarters and would not be "a major factor this quarter." CFO Bret Johnsen had said SpaceX still expects fourth-quarter capital expenditure of $35 billion to $40 billion. Reuters reported earlier this month that SpaceX was in talks with banks and asset managers to raise $40 billion to buy Nvidia (NVDA.O) chips.

item.title: Musk's grim outlook hits neoclouds as debt concerns mount
item.description: Shares of neocloud companies declined on Monday after SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said the sector could face consolidation and failures, adding to concerns over a widening gap between AI infrastructure investment and revenue generation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Shares of neocloud companies declined on Monday after SpaceX CEO [USN:L6N46B085 TEXT:"Elon Musk said"] the sector could face consolidation and failures, adding to concerns over a widening gap between AI infrastructure investment and revenue generation. CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , which has become a poster child for mounting concerns over heavy AI spending, declined 1.6%, while Nebius Group (NBIS.O) fell 4% and IREN (IREN.O) lost 1.5%. Shares of Applied Digital (APLD.O) shed 2%. In a social media post on Sunday, Musk said that neocloud companies would face significant consolidation and failures, adding that SpaceX (SPCX.O) would not buy any neocloud companies, calling it "pointless". "200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many," he said. "Musk is correct. You're going to need another source of revenue and profits in order to finance these projects moving forward. The cost of capital is too high to make the returns attractive," said Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital in New York. In an email to Reuters, a CoreWeave spokesperson said that the company continues to see opportunities to finance its growth, underscored by qualities such as "differentiated technology". Musk was [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"not alone"] in flagging the risks to the sector. Earlier this month, research firm Gartner said CoreWeave was at the top of the 100-odd neoclouds most exposed to the increasing leverage, and added that 80% of the companies could cease independent operations by 2032. Some brokerages expect AI spending to shoot past a trillion dollars next year, adding to investor concerns about the repercussions of severe dependence on debt, at a time when AI assets face rapid depreciation and markets price in more interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve. Bonds of Nebius maturing in 2034 and those of CoreWeave expiring in 2033 have hit record lows on the concerns. CoreWeave, Nebius, Applied Digital and TeraWulf have reported quarterly losses over the past one year, while IREN has not turned a profit in the past three quarters, raising scrutiny over profitability. Shares of CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN have fallen more than 30% this month alone. Investors betting on their fall have raked in at least [USN:L4N4681E0 TEXT:"$6 billion"] in paper profits.

item.title: Verizon logra su mejor captación de clientes móviles en cinco años y eleva sus previsiones anuales
item.description: Verizon registró un alza del 1,5% en sus ingresos operativos, hasta US$34.300 millones, y una ganancia por acción ajustada de US$1,31, por encima de las previsiones de Wall Street.
item.dc:creator: Kelcee Griffis
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Verizon Communications Inc. ( VZ ) registró en el tercer trimestre su mejor resultado de los últimos cinco años en cuanto a la captación de clientes de telefonía móvil, superando en más del doble las previsiones de los analistas, lo que indica que el primer año del plan de reestructuración del CEO, Dan Schulman, está dando sus frutos. El mayor proveedor de telefonía móvil de Estados Unidos registró un aumento neto de 406.000 líneas telefónicas mensuales en el periodo que finalizó el 30 de septiembre, una cifra muy superior a las previsiones de Wall Street, que apuntaban a 202.000 nuevas altas. La empresa también ha revisado al alza sus previsiones para todo el año en varios indicadores clave. Estos resultados significativamente superiores a lo previsto y estas previsiones optimistas se producen a pesar de que las cotizaciones bursátiles de los operadores de telefonía móvil se muestran inestables ante el temor de que las tres grandes empresas de telefonía móvil ya establecidas se enfrenten a una mayor competencia en el sector de la telefonía móvil por parte del próximo servicio Starlink Mobile de Elon Musk. Ver más: Verizon está en conversaciones para comprar el espectro inalámbrico de EchoStar Para mantener su competitividad, Verizon, con sede en Nueva York, está llevando a cabo una profunda reestructuración bajo la dirección de Schulman, quien, en el año que lleva en el cargo, ha suprimido miles de puestos de trabajo, ha anunciado un plan de servicios de telefonía móvil simplificado y ha introducido un nuevo programa de fidelización. Asimismo, ha esbozado una ambiciosa estrategia para integrar la inteligencia artificial en las operaciones de la empresa. Cuando Schulman asumió el cargo el pasado mes de octubre, Verizon se veía afectada por una ralentización en el crecimiento de sus abonados y un precio de las acciones a la baja. El antiguo CEO de PayPal Holdings Inc. ( PYPL ) se propuso recuperar la posición de liderazgo de Verizon en el mercado y se comprometió a dar prioridad a los clientes. Las acciones de Verizon han subido un 9% este año, superando las caídas registradas por AT&T Inc. ( T ) y T-Mobile US Inc. ( TMUS ). Los ingresos operativos totales aumentaron un 1,5%, hasta alcanzar los US$34.300 millones. El incremento de los ingresos por servicios de telefonía móvil y banda ancha compensó el descenso en las ventas de equipos, debido a que los clientes conservan sus teléfonos durante más tiempo. Verizon registró 314.000 altas netas de banda ancha, una cifra inferior a las 379.100 que esperaban los analistas. Ver más: SpaceX detalla sus planes para competir con AT&T, Verizon y T-Mobile en EE.UU. La ganancia por acción ajustada aumentó un 8,3% interanual, hasta situarse en US$1,31. Esta cifra contrasta con la previsión media de los analistas, que se situaba en US$1,28, según datos recopilados por Bloomberg. La empresa revisó al alza sus previsiones para todo el año en cuanto a altas netas mensuales de telefonía, beneficios, flujo de caja libre y crecimiento de los ingresos por servicios móviles y de banda ancha. La empresa espera ahora alcanzar hasta 1,2 millones de nuevas líneas telefónicas mensuales, frente a la previsión anterior de hasta 1 millón. Persisten grandes interrogantes sobre las ambiciones de SpaceX de convertirse en un cuarto competidor en el sector de la telefonía móvil, lo que supondría una mayor competencia por los clientes. Las acciones de Verizon y sus competidores cayeron la semana pasada después de que Bloomberg informara de que SpaceX está buscando un número significativo de emplazamientos para torres de telefonía móvil, lo que supondría un paso importante hacia su objetivo. Ver más: Verizon supera expectativas de ingresos y eleva previsiones mientras avanza su reestructuración Verizon también anunció el lunes que firmó un acuerdo de infraestructura de inteligencia artificial con la unidad de Servicios Web de Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN ), por un valor superior a los US$2.000 millones. Verizon es la segunda de las principales empresas de telecomunicaciones en publicar sus resultados del tercer trimestre. La semana pasada, AT&T Inc. obtuvo unos resultados financieros en general positivos, pero sus acciones cayeron después de que Musk reafirmara su intención de convertir a SpaceX en un “importante operador de telefonía móvil”. T-Mobile le seguirá con su informe el miércoles, tras el cierre del mercado. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Regeneron extends US agreement for additional supply of Ebola treatment
item.description: Regeneron said on Monday it extended its agreement with a US health authority to provide additional supply of its Ebola treatment, amid a growing outbreak in Africa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Regeneron (REGN.O) said on Monday it extended its agreement with a US health authority to provide additional supply of its Ebola treatment, amid a growing outbreak in Africa. Here are some details: The new agreement with the US Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, expanding a 2020 contract, will see Regeneron supply doses of its drug Inmazeb through 2031 for about $270 million The US Food and Drug Administration approved Inmazeb in 2020 for the treatment of infection caused by Zaire ebolavirus The current Ebola outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved specific antiviral treatment or licensed vaccine Regeneron said it is testing its experimental therapy, maftivimab, as a potential treatment for the Bundibugyo virus The outbreak, first reported in the Democratic Republic of Congo in May, has now spread to four countries across East, Central and West Africa — the widest geographic spread of any Ebola outbreak on the continent to date The current outbreak has infected nearly 10,000 people and killed more than 4,800 in Congo The disease can cause fever, vomiting, diarrhea and, in severe cases, internal and external bleeding
