Pennant needed more than 50 stitches after the incident and the 43-year-old posted a photo on social media showing his right leg heavily bandaged. "So I was attacked by a German Shepherd, I tried to protect (my dog) King but the dog got my leg," Pennant, who retired in 2018, wrote on Instagram.

item.title: Ovintiv to buy Logan Energy for $890 million, expanding Montney oil position
item.description: Oil and gas producer Ovintiv said on Monday it would acquire Canadian producer Logan Energy in an all-cash deal valuing the company at about $890 million, including debt.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oil and gas producer Ovintiv (OVV.N) said on Monday it would acquire Canadian producer Logan Energy (LGN.V) in an all-cash deal valuing the company at about $890 million, including debt. Here are more details: Ovintiv would pay C$1.40 ($0.9986) per share for Logan The deal would add about 266,000 net acres in the oil-rich Montney region and roughly 20,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day of production Ovintiv said the acquisition would add about 420 net drilling locations, including 220 premium-return wells The deal would also help generate annual cost synergies of roughly $60 million The deal is expected to close early in the first quarter of 2027 The assets include two oil batteries and stakes in two gas-processing facilities, which Ovintiv said should support margins and future production growth As part of the deal, Logan will spin off its newly formed subsidiary, Logan Oil Corp, to its shareholders Logan shareholders will also receive shares in spun-out Logan Oil Corp, initially valued at about C$0.08 per Logan share, and warrants, bringing total consideration to about C$1.48 per share In 2024, Ovintiv agreed to buy Paramount Resources' Montney assets for $2.38 billion while selling its Utah Uinta operations to FourPoint Resources for $2 billion ($1 = 1.4020 Canadian dollars)

item.title: Brasil tem menor saldo em transações correntes em 2 anos nos 12 meses até setembro
item.description: O déficit em transações correntes do Brasil diminuiu para 2,33% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) nos 12 meses até setembro, de 2,50% do PIB no mês anterior, mostraram dados do Banco Central nesta segunda-feira, atingindo o menor nível em dois anos, ajudado por um superávit comercial mais forte.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O déficit em transações correntes do Brasil diminuiu para 2,33% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) nos 12 meses até setembro, de 2,50% do PIB no mês anterior, mostraram dados do Banco Central nesta segunda-feira, atingindo o menor nível em dois anos, ajudado por um superávit comercial mais forte. Em setembro, as transações correntes da maior economia da América Latina registraram déficit de US$5,1 bilhões, enquanto economistas consultados em pesquisa da Reuters esperavam saldo negativo de US$5,0 bilhões. (BRCURA=ECI) Depois de aumentar acentuadamente em 2025, o déficit em transações correntes do Brasil acumulado em 12 meses vem apresentando melhora constante, apoiado por um superávit comercial crescente, impulsionado pela forte alta dos preços do petróleo, uma vez que o país é exportador líquido da commodity. O fortalecimento da balança comercial brasileira mais do que compensou o aumento dos déficits nas contas de serviços e de renda, que também apresentaram deterioração em setembro. O investimento direto no país (IDP) somou US$11,294 bilhões em setembro, superando amplamente os US$6,500 bilhões esperados pelos economistas na pesquisa da Reuters. (BRFDI=ECI) Nos 12 meses até setembro, o IDP subiu para 3,43% do PIB, ante 3,39% no mês anterior, permanecendo bem acima do déficit em transações correntes e indicando que os fluxos de capital de longo prazo continuaram financiando integralmente o déficit externo.

item.title: CNA Explains: Why are the Houthis targeting Saudi airports?
item.description: Saudi Arabia's main international airport in Riyadh has been a repeated target of attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels. CNA looks at why the Houthis are repeatedly targeting Saudi civilian infrastructure, and what this means for travel in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: CNA

CNA Explains: Why are the Houthis targeting Saudi airports?

Saudi Arabia's main international airport in Riyadh has been a repeated target of attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels. CNA looks at why the Houthis are repeatedly targeting Saudi civilian infrastructure, and what this means for travel in the Middle East.

Smoke and flames rise from King Khalid Airport after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis said they attacked the airport, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Oct 8, 2026, in this screengrab obtained from a social media video. (Image: Social Media via Reuters)

FAST

Saudi Arabia's main international airport in Riyadh has become a repeated target of attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels, disrupting flights and raising concerns about the security of civilian aviation in the kingdom. On Monday (Oct 26), the Saudi-led military coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the Houthis towards Riyadh, after the Iran-backed group claimed another attack on King Khalid International Airport. The latest incident came as flights resumed at the airport following weeks of disruption, with the Houthis warning airlines and travellers that the facility remained "unsafe" and a "military target". But the Houthis' attacks on Saudi airports are not new. As far back as November 2017, the group fired a ballistic missile towards King Khalid International Airport, which Saudi authorities said they intercepted.

In June 2019, a missile struck Abha International Airport in southern Saudi Arabia, injuring 26 civilians. The latest escalation has been particularly deadly. Earlier this month, an attack on Riyadh airport killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 , marking the deadliest such incident in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade. The attacks have disrupted travel plans for thousands of passengers, forced the postponement of Saudi Arabia's flagship investment conference until 2027 and cast uncertainty over the kingdom's ambitions to become a global tourism and business hub . CNA looks at why the Houthis are repeatedly targeting Saudi civilian infrastructure, and what this means for travel in the Middle East.

Houthi activists stand on a platform against a banner depicting Houthi missiles at an anti-Saudi rally amid an escalation with the kingdom, in Sanaa, Yemen on Jul 31, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Khaled Abdullah)

Why are the Houthis targeting airports? Airports are among a country's most strategically and economically important infrastructure, making them particularly disruptive targets during a conflict. The Houthis' raids on Saudi airports are part of a wider series of attacks on the kingdom's infrastructure, including on oil tankers and pumping stations. Missiles have also been fired towards the Saudi cities of Taif and Yanbu. The latter is a major oil export hub on the Red Sea coast that has allowed Riyadh to bypass Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The Houthis have described Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport as a military target and warned airlines against using it. However, the group's claims do not by themselves establish that the airport is a lawful military target under international humanitarian law. United Nations secretary-general António Guterres has called for an immediate halt to attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, saying that they violate international law.  Besides Riyadh, airports in Abha, Dammam, Najran and Jizan have also come under attack. The Houthis' targeting of critical infrastructure bears similarities to tactics used by their main backer, Iran, which has also launched attacks on infrastructure across Gulf Arab states.

Related:

Flights resume at Riyadh airport as Houthis attack Saudi Arabia

CNA Explains: How the Houthis could threaten the Red Sea and shape the Iran war

What triggered the latest escalation? The conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis dates back to 2015, when Riyadh led a military intervention in Yemen against the Iran-backed group. A United Nations-brokered truce in April 2022 brought a significant reduction in hostilities, including cross-border attacks. Although the ceasefire formally expired six months later, a relative calm largely held. Tensions flared again in July 2026 when the Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of launching airstrikes on Sanaa International Airport in Yemen's capital. Yemen's internationally recognised government's defence ministry said the strikes were intended to prevent an Iranian aircraft from landing at the airport. The Houthis subsequently launched missile and drone attacks on Abha International Airport, with no casualties reported. The group also declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began targeting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before launching a major offensive in September in which they seized Yemeni government-held territory along the Red Sea coast. The Houthis have also reported frequent Saudi airstrikes on areas under their control.

What impact are these attacks having on Saudi Arabia? The Houthi attacks have severely disrupted Saudi Arabia's aviation sector, forcing Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport to close for two weeks before resuming operations on Sunday (Oct 25). The fallout has extended beyond aviation, with several major international events cancelled, postponed or relocated over security concerns. Saudi Arabia has postponed its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference until 2027, while organisers of the prestigious motor sport race Dakar Rally on Sunday said it would move to a different location.  Golf's Asian Tour postponed the Saudi International indefinitely and cycling's Urban World Championships was cancelled earlier this month, while the tennis tournament Six Kings Slam was postponed to December. These disruptions come as Saudi Arabia pursues its Vision 2030 plan to diversify its economy.  Prolonged instability could undermine investor confidence and make it harder for it to attract international visitors, businesses and major events. The country's energy infrastructure has also come under threat. In September, Saudi Arabia temporarily shut down its 1,200km East-West pipeline as a precaution after a drone attack that Riyadh and Baghdad said originated in Iraq. The pipeline has served as a key route for Middle East oil exports amid the war-related disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. On Oct 24, the Houthis claimed to have targeted the pipeline, crude oil pumping stations, an Aramco facility in Yanbu and the Rabigh refinery. Saudi Arabia has not confirmed those claims.

Related:

US orders diplomats to depart Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes

Saudi says intercepted Houthi missile, blasts heard in capital

What is the official advice about travelling to Saudi Arabia? Amid the escalating violence, the United States has ordered some diplomats and their family members to leave its missions in Saudi Arabia , and plans to withdraw family members from several other US missions in the region. Washington had returned some diplomatic personnel to the region in recent months, after many were pulled out following Iranian attacks on US facilities when the US-Israeli war against Iran began in late February. On Singapore's part, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has advised Singaporeans to defer all travel to Saudi Arabia , citing an increase in missile and drone attacks targeting civilian aviation and energy infrastructure. The Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) has also advised Singaporeans planning to perform Umrah to consider postponing their trips to Saudi Arabia . Umrah is a voluntary pilgrimage to Mecca that Muslims can undertake at any time of the year. Despite the advisories, some Singaporeans are pressing ahead with their pilgrimage plans. Some families CNA spoke to earlier this month said that they were adopting adopt a " wait-and-see” approach, while others have had their pilgrimage cancelled.

Related:

Some Singapore pilgrims press ahead with Umrah plans despite advisory, others face cancellations

Singaporeans advised to defer all travel to Saudi Arabia amid heightened security risks: MFA

Singapore condemns Houthi attacks on civilian aviation infrastructure in Saudi Arabia

Why are the Houthis able to strike Riyadh so often? Iran has provided the Houthis with weapons, funding and training for more than a decade, although Tehran denies arming the group in violation of a United Nations arms embargo. Despite Iran facing its own financial and military strains due to war and sanctions, the Houthis have learned - with Iranian help - how to assemble their own weapons, including drones and missiles, experts interviewed by Reuters said. Iran's Revolutionary Guards and members of Iran's other ally, Lebanese Hezbollah, initially gave the Houthis knowledge of missile systems and their operation, Andreas Krieg, senior security studies lecturer at King's College London told Reuters. "Former Yemeni military engineers and a growing generation of locally trained specialists have helped institutionalise these capabilities," he said. "Tehran has not simply supplied the Houthis with weapons. It has helped create an indigenous military-industrial learning process that becomes progressively harder to dismantle, even if direct Iranian supply routes are disrupted." This has made the Houthis one of Iran's most cost-effective and valuable regional military allies. The group has also reportedly turned to artificial intelligence to enhance its weapons capabilities. Anthropic said last month that "a cell of threat actors based in northern Yemen" had used its Claude AI assistant to help develop software for a guided rocket, a planned ballistic missile with a range of more than 2,000km and a missile variant incorporating a hypersonic glide vehicle. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia's air defences face mounting pressure from repeated missile and drone attacks, even as its US ally grapples with demands on its own air defence resources amid the war with Iran.

Source: CNA/Agencies/nh

item.title: Senior doctors in England set to strike over pay offer in November
item.description: Senior hospital doctors in England are set to stage a two-day strike in November, the British Medical Association said on Monday, following a government recommendation of a below-inflation pay rise.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Senior hospital doctors in England are set to stage a two-day strike in November, the British Medical Association said on Monday, following a government recommendation of a below-inflation pay rise. The strike, due to take place on November 25 and 26, is the latest example of disputes over pay and working conditions across Britain's National Health Service which have led to more than a dozen rounds of industrial action since 2023. The government's proposal of a 2.4% rise to the body that sets doctors' pay for the 2027/2028 financial year, is a "significant real-terms pay cut by all current measures of inflation," the BMA said. It noted that senior doctors had seen a 25% cut to their pay in real terms over the last 17 years. The strike can be avoided if Britain's health minister commits to adequately funded formal negotiations on both pay and working conditions, the BMA said in a statement. The headline rate of CPI inflation in September was 3.5%, the Office for National Statistics said [USN:L8N46708O TEXT:"on Wednesday"]. Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said the BMA's decision was "very disappointing" following what she called constructive discussions between her department, the NHS and the BMA. "With colleagues across the NHS, I am determined to support staff and patients through the tough winter period," she said. "I hope the BMA will stay united with us in that effort, and not take irresponsible action that would place our health service under even greater pressure at this crucial time." The government had said in its evidence to the Review Body on Doctors' and Dentists' Remuneration, published on October 19, that its plan for a 2.4% rise did not have to make "trade offs against headline government health commitments".

item.title: 楽天トラベル、顧客情報260万件に不正アクセス クレジットカード情報3.6万件
item.description: [東京 ２６日 ロイター] - 楽天グループは２６日、旅行予約サービス「楽天トラベル」の顧客情報最大２６０万件が不正...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
楽天トラベル、顧客情報260万件に不正アクセス　クレジットカード情報3.6万件 20:30 配信

２０２５年１０月撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Dado Ruvic/Illustration）

[東京 ２６日 ロイター] - 楽天グループは２６日、旅行予約サービス「楽天トラベル」の顧客情報最大２６０万件が不正アクセスを受けたと発表した。最大４万件については氏名やメールアドレス電話番号などが、うち最大３万６０００件はクレジットカード情報が不正アクセスを受けた。

クレジットカード情報には、発行者識別番号と下４桁、名義人名、有効期限、国際ブランド区分が含まれる。セキュリティコードは対象外だという。

不正アクセスを受けたのは、海外ホテル予約サイトのうち、シンガポール子会社が管理・運営する一部のページ。９月１０日に異常を検知し、１５日に原因を特定、１６日にシステム改修を完了したとしている。

また、楽天トラベルの多言語予約サイトも１０月２０日に不正アクセスの可能性を検知。最大８６万件の顧客メールアドレスと社内用識別番号が不正アクセスの対象となった。

item.title: Itaú compra la startup brasileña de IA NeoSpace por US$580 millones para personalizar sus servicios
item.description: La adquisición de NeoSpace, que se pagará íntegramente en efectivo, permitirá al mayor banco de América Latina por activos combinar la tecnología de la startup con su experiencia en servicios financie ...
item.dc:creator: Matheus Piovesana
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — Itaú Unibanco Holding SA ( ITUB ), el mayor banco de América Latina por activos, anunció la adquisición de la startup brasileña de inteligencia artificial NeoSpace AI Technologies Ltda., en una operación por valor de 2.900 millones de reales (US$580 millones) destinada a impulsar los objetivos tecnológicos del banco. La operación ayudará a Itaú a desarrollar sus propios modelos de inteligencia artificial mediante la combinación de la tecnología de NeoSpace con los conocimientos técnicos del banco en materia de servicios financieros, según indicó Itaú el lunes en un comunicado. La adquisición, que se realizará íntegramente en efectivo, permitirá a la startup mantener una gestión y una estructura autónomas, con su fundador, Bruno Pierobon, como CEO. Ver más: Itaú compra 35% de Prisma Capital para expandirse en activos alternativos en Brasil NeoSpace, fundada en 2023, desarrolla inteligencia artificial que identifica patrones y relaciones complejas en grandes conjuntos de datos, según ha indicado el banco. Itaú ya es cliente de la empresa y lideró una ronda de inversión de US$18 millones a principios de 2025. El banco considera que los modelos de NeoSpace son una vía para personalizar su servicio al cliente. Itaú ha realizado importantes inversiones para modernizar sus plataformas, en un momento en que el sector financiero brasileño intenta mantenerse al día con una industria fintech muy desarrollada. En 2024 unificó diferentes aplicaciones móviles en una sola, a medida que los clientes dejaban de acudir a las sucursales físicas y el banco buscaba una oportunidad para reforzar sus vínculos con los clientes que solo utilizan un producto. Ver más: Itaú recorta su previsión de ingresos por comisiones ante la volatilidad del mercado Esta iniciativa tiene como objetivo aumentar la cantidad de datos a los que el banco tiene acceso a la hora de analizar el riesgo de cada cliente, pero también garantizar que dichos clientes se mantengan fieles al banco en un sentido más amplio, una estrategia que los bancos tradicionales y las empresas de tecnología financiera de otros lugares también están tratando de aplicar a medida que se intensifica la competencia. El banco ha realizado otras adquisiciones en el sector tecnológico durante la última década. En 2019, anunció que había acordado la compra de Zup, una startup fundada también por Pierobon que ofrece servicios para integrar sistemas de nuevo desarrollo en estructuras heredadas. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

AI cuts some Deutsche Bank corporate loan decisions to minutes

The logo of Deutsche Bank is seen on the roof of a building outside a Deutsche Bank branch office in Malaga, Spain, April 24, 2024. REUTERS/Jon Nazca

FAST

FRANKFURT, Oct 26 : AI is helping Deutsche Bank cut decisions for some smaller corporate lending from weeks to just minutes, its new technology chief Marie-Jeanne Deverdun told Reuters. The project, which went live in the summer, also reduces the time taken to make some lending decisions for multinational corporations from months to weeks, said Deverdun, who joined Deutsche Bank's management board this year. "For smaller corporates, which are less complicated in their setup and their legal structure, we're talking weeks to minutes," Deverdun said in an interview. Deverdun said Deutsche Bank is also preparing for a future when its AI agents will interact directly with clients' own agents, as lenders are drawn into the debate among technology leaders over whether AI development is moving too fast.

"We are watching that debate carefully. These are very valid concerns, and, obviously, the management of cyber risk is my number one priority," she said. "We're spending a lot of resources and budget to continue to protect the bank from those new technologies and threats," she added. Banking regulators are stepping up efforts to contain growing AI risk as lenders race to deploy the technology while balancing questions over returns and security threats. Deutsche Bank, Germany's largest lender, plans more than €2.5 billion ($2.80 billion) in tech spending between 2026 and 2028. By comparison, JPMorgan is budgeting $20 billion for 2026. Banks hope AI will trim costs and boost productivity. Britain's Barclays said last week it was cutting around 5,000 jobs or 5 per cent of its workforce this year as it uses the technology. Citigroup has said AI was now developing products at lower cost and up to 40 per cent faster. Major US banks, meanwhile, have begun blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside customer accounts in response to concerns that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth. Deutsche Bank CEO Christian Sewing has said he wants to make Deutsche "a truly AI-powered bank" after his predecessor said in 2015 its systems were "disjointed, cumbersome and far too often just plain incompatible". After the Ukraine war began, Deutsche Bank had to move its tech staff out of Russia and it is still streamlining an array of platforms, although it has cited some recent progress. Deverdun said Deutsche Bank had built an internal AI platform known as ADA, named after computing pioneer Ada Lovelace, to develop, monitor and control AI agents. ADA allows the bank to oversee agent activity, manage risk and switch between AI models as technology evolves, she said. "We're already preparing for an agentic economy where our agents interact with the agents of our clients with clear accountability and the right controls," she added. ($1 = 0.8937 euros)

item.title: FedEx appoints Jamere Jackson as chief financial officer
item.description: FedEx on Monday appointed Jamere Jackson as chief financial officer, effective November 30.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: FedEx (FDX.N) on Monday appointed Jamere Jackson as chief financial officer, effective November 30. Jackson will step down as CFO of AutoZone (AZO.N) on November 25. “During Jamere’s six-year tenure at AutoZone, he was a key contributor in helping shape the strategies we implemented to drive record sales, earnings," the automotive parts retailer's CEO Phil Daniele said. Jackson previously served as CFO of car rental firm Hertz (HTZ.O) and TV ratings company Nielsen. He also held senior finance roles at industrial giant General Electric (GE.N) and is a board member and audit committee chair at drugmaker Eli Lilly (LLY.N) . At FedEx, Jackson succeeds Claude Russ, who has been the interim finance chief since June 1, after John Dietrich [USN:L4N40W1MX TEXT:"stepped down"], following FedEx Freight's (FDXF.N) spinoff into a publicly traded company. FedEx is set to report third-quarter results on Wednesday.

item.title: 中国人民銀、ノンバンクの大量解約に備え流動性供給制度
item.description: [北京／上海 ２６日 ロイター] - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）は２６日、大規模な解約に直面するノンバンク金融機関に緊...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国人民銀、ノンバンクの大量解約に備え流動性供給制度 20:21 配信

北京の中国人民銀行本部、2025年5月撮影 REUTERS/Tingshu Wang

[北京／上海 ２６日 ロイター] - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）は２６日、大規模な解約に直面するノンバンク金融機関に緊急流動性を供給するスワップ制度の創設を発表した。国内債券市場の安定維持への取り組みの一環。

人民銀によると、資産運用会社が集団的な流動性リスクに直面した場合や債券市場がシステミックなストレスにさらされた時などに発動する。

こうした状況下では、金融システム上重要な理財部門や投資信託運用会社とその親会社が人民銀から中央銀行手形を借り入れ、市場でのレポ取引を通じて資金を調達できる。調達資金で適格債券や、解約に直面する自社の投資信託商品の受益権を購入し、これらの資産を人民銀に担保として差し入れる仕組みだ。

人民銀の潘功勝総裁は先週、国家金融監督管理総局と中国証券監督管理委員会と連携し、ノンバンク金融機関の大規模な解約に対応する流動性支援策を導入すると表明していた。

item.title: Ukrainian who fled Oleshky views US-brokered ceasefire with deep scepticism
item.description: Six weeks ago, Vitaly, his wife Iryna, their 13-year-old son Vlad left the besieged town of Oleshky in Russian-occupied Ukraine to escape what they feared was certain death by starvation.
item.dc:creator: Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Six weeks ago, Vitaly, his wife Iryna, their 13-year-old son Vlad and their cat left the besieged town of Oleshky in Russian-occupied Ukraine to escape what they feared was certain death by starvation. Now back in Ukraine after a gruelling journey via Russia and Belarus, Vitaly views with deep scepticism a temporary ceasefire in his native town set to begin on Tuesday to allow evacuations and send in supplies. Russia and Ukraine reached the [USN:L1N4690MZ TEXT:"agreement"], announced by the White House on Friday, with the mediation of US first lady Melania Trump and after additional involvement from [USN:L8N4651KU TEXT:"Pope Leo"]. After more than four years living under Russian occupation in a town on the front line of fierce fighting with Ukrainian forces, Vitaly is not optimistic that the ceasefire can hold for long or the humanitarian situation significantly improve. "Regarding the truce, I'm very sceptical about all this," said Vitaly, 55, who declined to give his last name for security reasons because his relatives were still living in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. "I have a lot of respect for Melania Trump, but she does not influence dictator (Russian President Vladimir) Putin," he told Reuters, sitting in a modern apartment in the Kyiv region where his family has temporarily settled. He said many of those remaining in [USN:L2N46C0BA TEXT:"Oleshky"] are sick or elderly and it would be difficult for them to relocate. Ukraine and Russia blame each other for the humanitarian crisis in Oleshky. Drones present the greatest threat to civilian life, and the town is within easy reach of unmanned aerial vehicles belonging to both armies. Because supplies are running out and the route north is blocked by the Dnipro river, some residents have walked 20 km (12 miles) to the next village to stock up on food and water. The journey is fraught with danger and locals call it the [USN:L8N45K1N1 TEXT:""road of death""]. TEMPORARY CEASEFIRE AGREED Ukraine and Russia agreed to a temporary ceasefire around Oleshky that is expected to begin on October 27 at 3 a.m. Kyiv time (0100 GMT). Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said that Kyiv hoped it would be possible to open up Oleshky, provide access for food and medicine and allow people to leave the area. The Kremlin has said that all civilians wishing to leave Oleshky would be allowed to do so and that the evacuation was expected to take at least several days. Oleshky, a small town across the Dnipro from Ukraine's regional hub of Kherson, had a prewar population of some 24,000. It is still home to around 1,700 residents, including about 35 children, according to the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine. UNDER RUSSIAN CONTROL Russian troops have occupied Oleshky since the first days of the full-scale invasion in February 2022. It has been largely cut off from running water, electricity, gas and central heating since the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam in 2023 and subsequent flooding of nearby areas. As the war ground on, the humanitarian crisis deepened. By the middle of last year, the constant threat of drones choked off supply lines, causing food scarcity. And from late May this year, the situation became severe, according to residents Reuters has spoken to. Vitaly said his family survived for weeks by rationing a single cup of rice or buckwheat a day, occasionally adding a cucumber or tomato mixed with purslane, a common wild weed. During the summer months, some residents could sell vegetables, but prices were unaffordable for most. A kilo of tomatoes cost about 1,500 roubles ($18.50). To buy eggs, you needed to know the right people and 10 eggs would cost around 3,000 roubles, Vitaly recalled. No one was willing to sell potatoes. After counting their meagre food stocks, and remembering last winter when the temperature in their apartment dropped to between 1 and 3 degrees Celsius (34 and 37 degrees Fahrenheit), they decided to leave. "You look at what remained from your food supplies and realize that there is only one way for you — to go on foot or die of hunger," Vitaly said. Their home in Oleshky had been damaged by a drone, Iryna said, and they did not have anything left there. ARDUOUS ESCAPE On September 13, the family joined a small party of eight people and set out on foot. They walked for more than 20 km to the village of Radensk. The road was heavily mined, and drones were flying overhead. Vitaly said they saw the body of a woman lying on the road as they passed by. They took with them only their autumn clothes, Vlad's teddy bear, the cat and a handful of family photos. They travelled from Radensk by bus deeper into Russian-occupied Ukraine, crossed into Russia after lengthy questioning by authorities at the border, and finally Belarus before returning to Ukrainian-controlled territory on September 17. The family has spent the past several weeks settling into a new routine in the Kyiv region. One of their first purchases was a bag of potatoes, bought to cook mashed potatoes for their son. "The kid will be in school. We will be working. My wife needs to get her health back on track a bit," Vitaly said. As for his own future: "I will either join the army or will try to find a position somewhere here with weapon producers to help our country defeat its enemies."

item.title: Meta eyes record $95 billion equity raise to fund AI expansion
item.description: Meta Platforms said on Monday it plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising, as the social media giant spends aggressively on its AI infrastructure expansion.
item.dc:creator: Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: Meta Platforms (META.O) said on Monday it plans to raise up to $95 billion in its largest-ever equity fundraising, as the social media giant spends aggressively on its AI infrastructure expansion. The Facebook parent has launched public offerings worth about $35 billion in common and preferred stock, and said it also plans to launch a separate at-the-market share sale program worth up to $60 billion. The company will launch the larger share sale program after its new non-voting Class C shares begin trading, which is expected in the first quarter of 2027, but said it has not yet finalized its timing and terms of the sale. Meta's fundraising plan, among the biggest by an AI company, has also drawn interest of up to $5 billion in total from Nvidia (NVDA.O) , Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) and Broadcom (AVGO.O) for Class A shares. Their funding interest adds to concerns about an increasingly circular flow of capital in the AI industry, as chip suppliers help finance the expansion of one of their biggest customers. Meta has been pouring money into chips and data centers to compete better with OpenAI and Anthropic. "We expect investors to continue to question the financing and potential for future capital raises," William Blair analysts said in a note. "Overall, we believe the financing reinforces both Meta's confidence in the long-term returns from AI investment and the increasingly capital-intensive nature of pursuing that opportunity." The company's shares fell about 1.4% in morning trading. The latest fundraising further underscores a shift among big technology companies increasingly [USN:L6N3WU0Q5 TEXT:"tapping debt markets and raising equity"] to bolster their AI infrastructure, having previously relied on cash to fund their investments. Earlier this year, [USN:L4N42B1AK TEXT:"Alphabet increased the size"] of its equity offerings to $84.75 billion. Separately on Monday, SpaceX said an affiliate of Apollo Global Management (APO.N) will buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the rockets-to-AI firm, in a deal with total principal payments of [USN:L6N46C0RJ TEXT:"about $40 billion"]. META'S AI SPENDING IS BURNING CASH Meta has committed to spend about $825 billion in the future, primarily driven by its growing investments in data centers, AI-related infrastructure and cloud computing power. But the aggressive expansion has eroded its historically strong free cash flow. The company reported a $2.12 billion cash burn in the third quarter, its first negative free cash flow in over a decade, compared with a positive cash flow of $10.63 billion a year ago. Still, the early popularity of [USN:L6N4500XV TEXT:"its consumer-focused AI agent Muse"] and release of a competitive new [USN:L4N45Y13Q TEXT:"series of AI models"] have helped partly justify Meta's aggressive investments. "We believe that Meta will ultimately produce a profitable AI business and its returns longer-term should help the company diversify, although the path may not be linear," William Blair analysts said. The company had cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of $82.45 billion and long-term debt of $80.92 billion as of September 30, according to its latest quarterly filing. Last week, Meta raised the lower end of its annual [USN:L4N4671S3 TEXT:"capital expenditure"] forecast to a range of $135 billion to $145 billion. The company has said it would issue Class C common stock in January 2027, effectively resulting in a two-for-one split, to fund acquisitions and retain top talent while maintaining CEO Mark Zuckerberg's control. Meta [USN:L6N46801B TEXT:"agreed to grant Zuckerberg Class C shares"] that he can sell to help pay a potential California billionaire wealth tax, in exchange for a commitment to keep him in California.

item.title: Verizon lifts annual forecasts, signs more than $2 billion AI infrastructure deal with AWS
item.description: Verizon raised its annual forecast for wireless subscriber additions on Monday, betting on strong demand for its simplified plans, and signed an AI infrastructure deal worth more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Verizon (VZ.N) raised its annual forecast for wireless subscriber additions on Monday, betting on strong demand for its simplified plans, and signed an AI infrastructure deal worth more than $2 billion with Amazon Web Services. For the third quarter, the telecom carrier reported nearly double the analysts' estimate for gains in monthly-bill paying wireless subscribers at 406,000, against Visible Alpha expectations of 209,439. Verizon now expects to add between 1.1 million and 1.2 million postpaid phone subscribers this year compared with earlier projections of 750,000 to 1 million It also raised its full-year adjusted earnings per share forecast to $5.04 to $5.06, from $4.99 to $5.04 earlier However, third-quarter revenue of $34.3 billion fell short of analyst estimates of $34.74 billion, according to LSEG data Revenue was pressured by lower device upgrade volumes after Verizon began cutting device subsidies. Verizon expects this trend to continue in the fourth quarter. Verizon shares fell 2.5% in early trading Under its deal with Amazon's (AMZN.O) cloud unit, Verizon will provide high-capacity fiber-optic connectivity for AWS data centers CEO Dan Schulman said in the post-earnings call the company was in talks with additional hyperscalers, neocloud providers and large enterprise clients to supply dark or lit fiber connectivity Meanwhile, commenting on SpaceX’s (SPCX.O) plans to enter the mobile market, Schulman said building a competing terrestrial network would take four to six years and cost $300 billion to $500 billion Verizon would be "ferociously competitive" once SpaceX enters the market, he added

item.title: Aguinaldo 2026 en México: quiénes lo cobran en noviembre y la fecha límite del 20 de diciembre
item.description: El artículo 87 de la Ley Federal del Trabajo establece que los trabajadores tendrán derecho a un aguinaldo anual que deberá pagarse a más tardar el 20 de diciembre. Existen empresas que pagan el ...
item.dc:creator: Italia López
item.content:encoded: Ciudad de México — El fin de año se aproxima y con ello llega el esperado pago del aguinaldo, una prestación laboral de la que goza buena parte de los trabajadores del país. De acuerdo con la Ley Federal del Trabajo, tienen derecho al aguinaldo todas las personas trabajadoras, ya sea de base, de confianza, de planta, sindicalizadas, aquellas contratadas por obra, tiempo determinado, temporada, por tiempo indeterminado sujeto a prueba o sujeto a capacitación inicial, eventuales, comisionistas, agentes de comercio, de seguros, vendedores y otros similares. También tienen derecho a recibirlo las personas pensionadas del IMSS o del ISSSTE, mientras se hayan jubilado por Cesantía en edad avanzada o por vejez bajo la Ley del Seguro Social de 1973. El artículo 87 de la Ley Federal del Trabajo establece que los trabajadores tendrán derecho a un aguinaldo anual que deberá pagarse a más tardar el 20 de diciembre. Existen empresas que pagan el aguinaldo en la primera quincena de diciembre antes de que llegue el plazo legal. Otras lo depositan antes de la primera quincena de diciembre. Los pensionados del IMSS y del ISSSTE reciben su aguinaldo en noviembre. De acuerdo con el calendario de pagos a pensionados y jubilados del ISSSTE, el aguinaldo en 2026 se depositará en dos partes: un pago la primera quincena de noviembre y otro el 27 de noviembre. El IMSS menciona en su sitio que el aguinaldo se paga en el mes de noviembre. Para los trabajadores del Gobierno en dependencias federales y entidades paraestatales, el pago del aguinaldo podrá realizarse a partir del 10 de noviembre de 2026, de acuerdo con las disposiciones publicadas en el Diario Oficial de la Federación el 23 de octubre. Con información de Zenyazen Flores

item.title: France's Macron promises 'strong measures' to assuage protests
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron promised on Monday that his government would announce a package of measures in response to weeks of street protests over a broad set of grievances, while acknowledging the risk of more unrest ahead.
item.dc:creator: Crispian Balmer, Sudip Kar-Gupta
item.content:encoded: French President Emmanuel Macron promised on Monday that his government would announce a package of measures in response to weeks of street protests over a broad set of grievances, while acknowledging the risk of more unrest ahead. His prime minister, Sebastien Lecornu, is set to hold a news conference after a meeting with unions of high school students who want more resources for the education sector and an overhaul of a university admissions process they say embeds inequalities. "I have ... asked the government to respond to the legitimate demands that lie at the root of this social movement," Macron told reporters in Marseille, where he travelled to inspect the damage from earlier protests. Macron repeated what Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said earlier, that more unrest is expected next weekend. FAR-RIGHT GANGS CONFRONT FAR-LEFT ACTIVISTS The protests show little sign of easing [USN:L1N46608H TEXT:"after violence"] nine days ago engulfed dozens of cities, leading to fears the state had lost control of the streets. In response to the turmoil, the interior ministry deployed 70,000 police for Saturday's demonstrations, which unions called to denounce the high cost of living and public services. The movement has grown far beyond initial student discontent, drawing in trade unions and "yellow vest" activists, known for their high-visibility jackets and mass demonstrations against economic pressures including high fuel costs. Nunez said the huge police presence prevented a repeat of violence seen earlier this month, but asked by BFM TV on Monday whether he expected further disturbances during [USN:L5N46B02K TEXT:"demonstrations planned"] for October 31, he replied: "Clearly, yes." "Halloween evening is traditionally always a bit lively. We expect it to be complicated again," he added. Nunez said 1,435 people were arrested nationwide during Saturday's demonstrations and said police had also recorded a new phenomenon, with organised far-right gangs confronting far-left activists in several cities. "We knew there had been calls from numerous identity-based and nationalist movements to come out, officially, to defend businesses," he said. "In a number of cities, such as Nice and Montpellier, these groups arrived in organised formations, mainly to target the ultra-left movement." The government sought to portray Saturday's operation as evidence it had regained the upper hand, despite sporadic violence, especially in France's three largest cities — Paris, Marseille and Lyon. "The state prevailed this weekend. The state was strong," government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon told RTL radio. She said protesters had raised legitimate grievances that needed to be heard, but added that restoring calm was a prerequisite for meaningful negotiations. With his presidential mandate due to expire in April and public finances under severe strain, Macron has limited scope to defuse the crisis through the costly concessions that helped quell previous waves of unrest. Business leaders said the unrest was continuing to inflict heavy economic damage despite a calmer weekend. Alain Di Crescenzo, head of the CCI France network of chambers of commerce and industry, said many retailers had remained closed as a precaution after the violence of October 17, adding that sales had fallen by about 80%. "We have shopkeepers who are tired and demoralised, and we are killing local commerce," he told Radio Classique.

item.title: 独ＩＦＯ業況指数、10月90.2で予想以上に改善 先行きを楽観視
item.description:
Maria Martinez
[ベルリン ２６日 ロイター] - ドイツのＩＦＯ経済研究所が２６日発表した１０月の業況...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独ＩＦＯ業況指数、10月90.2で予想以上に改善　先行きを楽観視 19:50 配信

ベルリンの街並み、6月撮影 REUTERS/Fabrizio Bensch

Maria Martinez

[ベルリン ２６日 ロイター] - ドイツのＩＦＯ経済研究所が２６日発表した１０月の業況指数は、先行きへの楽観的な見方が強まったことで、市場予想以上に改善した。改善は６カ月連続。

業況指数は９０．２と、９月の８９．９から上昇した。ロイターがまとめたアナリスト予想は９０．０だった。

期待指数は９月の９０．４から９１．６に上昇した。

ＩＦＯのクレメンス・フュースト所長は「景気回復は続いている」と述べた。

ＶＰバンクのチーフエコノミスト、トーマス・ギッツェル氏によると、１０月の企業の先行きに対する楽観度は４年半超ぶりの高水準となった。

ドイツ政府は経済成長率予想を引き上げ２０２６年が１．３％、２７年が１．１％とした。４月時点では０．５％、０．９％と予想していた。

ハンブルク商業銀行のチーフエコノミスト、サイラス・デラルビア氏は「ＩＦＯ業況指数が６カ月連続で上昇したことは、数多くの逆風にもかかわらずドイツ経済が成長軌道にあることを示唆している」と述べた。

第３・四半期の成長率は３０日に発表される。

キャピタル・エコノミクスは、ここ数カ月でＩＦＯなど一部の企業調査が改善したものの、第３・四半期はゼロ成長にとどまったと予想している。ただ欧州担当チーフエコノミスト、アンドリュー・ケニンガム氏は「労働市場の回復の兆しや財政刺激策の継続と併せ、今回の調査は第３・四半期の一時的な低迷が一過性の要因にもよるもので、第４・四半期は成長を取り戻すというわれわれの見方を裏付けている」と述べた。

ＶＰバンクのギッツェル氏によると、景況感の改善は全て製造業によるもの。好調な受注と政府のインフラ基金の効果が表れ始め、製造業の景況感を明確に押し上げているという。一方でサービス業は企業の楽観的な見方が後退、家計の消費支出の低迷が原因とみられるという。

ＩＮＧのマクロ調査グローバル責任者、カーステン・ブジェスキ氏は「今回の指数は、ドイツ経済の先行きを巡り継続中の財政刺激策の効果が経済全体に一段と波及することが、引き続き期待されていることを示している」と述べた。

メルツ首相は経済再生に向け、通常予算とは別枠で５０００億ユーロ（５６００億ドル）規模のインフラ基金を創設した。また、軍備増強に向け、憲法に定める借り入れ制限「債務ブレーキ」を見直した。

＜現況判断は悪化＞

期待指数の上昇が業況指数全体を押し上げた一方、現況に対する評価はやや悪化した。現況指数は前月の８９．５から８８．８に低下した。

デラルビア氏は、原油・ガス価格の大幅な上昇が電力価格の上昇や株式市場のボラティリティーにもつながっており、企業に打撃を与えるのは間違いないと指摘。さらに「ドイツ企業にとって２番目に重要な輸出先であるフランス経済が、政治的混乱や債券市場の動揺によってほぼ停滞したままとなれば、その影響はドイツにも及ぶ」との見方を示した。

コメルツ銀行のエコノミスト、イェルク・クレーマー氏は、さまざまなリスクにもかかわらず、ドイツ経済の回復は続く公算が大きいと指摘。ただ「抜本的な改革の欠如、トランプ氏の関税、中国の輸出攻勢により、回復は緩やかなものにとどまるだろう」との見方を示した。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：円急伸で揺らぐキャリートレード、見つからない次の調達通貨 アングル：世界市場が当面向き合う6つのリスク、地政学や金融政策・ＡＩなど アングル：湾岸諸国、インフラ整備に重点投資　ホルムズ海峡封鎖で紛争耐性強化へ アングル：東京から欧州まで、猛暑で広がる男性の「短パン通勤」 焦点：仏、財政赤字巡り政局緊迫　大統領選控え市場の不安と格下げ警戒 最終更新: 10/26(月) 20:56 ロイター

item.title: 米年末商戦の配送料過去最高へ、軽油高騰にサーチャージ算出変更が拍車
item.description:
Lisa Baertlein
［ロサンゼルス ２６日 ロイター］ - 今年の米国年末商戦の小口貨物配送料金は過去最高と...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米年末商戦の配送料過去最高へ、軽油高騰にサーチャージ算出変更が拍車 19:47 配信

フェデックスの配送トラック、米ワシントンDCで2024年撮影 REUTERS/Benoit Tessier/File Photo

Lisa Baertlein

［ロサンゼルス　２６日　ロイター］ - 今年の米国年末商戦の小口貨物配送料金は過去最高となる見通しだ。ディーゼル燃料（軽油）価格の高騰でＵＰＳとフェデックスが燃油サーチャージを引き上げており、米小売業者に逆風が吹いている。しかし、配送コスト上昇は、単純に燃料価格の問題だけではなさそうだ。そこには運送会社のサーチャージ算出方法変更という要因が働いているという。

年末商戦に関連する荷物量は第４・四半期に倍増することもある。大手小売業者を含む荷主１８００社の匿名化データを分析したＴＤコーエン／ＡＦＳ貨物指数によると、同四半期の陸送料金は、ネット通販購入品を含め、前年同期比で５．８％上昇、速達便は１３．８％上昇する見通しだ。同指数は、小口貨物のコストは重量やサイズ、配送先によって異なるため、金額ではなく変化率を示している。

米エネルギー情報局（ＥＩＡ）によると、１０月１９日時点の米国の路上用ディーゼル燃料の平均価格は１ガロン＝６．２８ドルだった。米国とイスラエルが２月２８日にイランを攻撃して以降、６５％上昇したことになる。

ＡＦＳロジスティクスのチーフアナリティクスオフィサー、ミンシュ・ベイツ氏は「燃料は誰にとっても最大の関心事だが、良い材料は見当たらない」と述べた。

＜運送会社の算出方法変更がコスト押し上げ＞

小売業者が頭を痛める輸送コスト。拍車をかけているのは、運送会社の算出方法の変更だ。

ベイツ氏によると、燃油サーチャージコストのうち軽油価格の上昇による分は３０％弱にすぎない。ＵＰＳやフェデックスなど業界大手が算出方法を変更したことにより、サーチャージは燃料価格よりもはるかに速いペースで上昇し、燃料価格が上がらない場合でも上昇しているという。

例えば、２０２１年第１・四半期に軽油価格が２．９１ドルだった時、同指数で燃油サーチャージは基本配送料金の７．７５％だった。仮に軽油価格がこの水準まで下がったとしても、現在の燃油サーチャージは２３．７５％と約３倍になる。燃油サーチャージの算出方法の変更が運送会社の収入を増やし、小売業者のコストを押し上げる構図だ。

各社のサーチャージ表に基づくと、ＥＩＡの平均価格である６．２８ドルでは、ＵＰＳの燃油サーチャージは２９．５％、フェデックスは２９％となる。

ＵＰＳは、料金設定は同社の質の高いサービスとインフラ投資を反映していると説明した。フェデックスはコメント要請に応じていない。両社は今週、四半期決算を発表する予定だ。

重いサーチャージ負担を小売業者はただ受け入れているだけなのか。

オントラック、ゴーフォー、ユニユニ、ジツ、ビーホなどは急成長中の配送会社だ。配送追跡・管理会社シップマトリックスのサティッシュ・ジンデル社長によると、米国の人口の約７０％をカバーしており、年末商戦期の荷物量の増加に対応するため、輸送能力も増強している。「輸送費を減らしたい多くの荷主に採用されている」という。

とはいえ、こうした企業の一部も高額な燃油サーチャージを導入している。オントラックが公開しているサーチャージ表によると、１０月２５日までの１週間の同社の西海岸のサーチャージは２９．５％だった。

輸送コストを抑えるために、米郵政公社（ＵＳＰＳ）やアマゾン・ドット・コムの物流部門を使う手もある。ＵＳＰＳは４月、大半の荷物に初めて８％の燃油サーチャージを課した。アマゾンも同じ月に、出品者向けのフルフィルメント手数料に３．５％の燃料・物流関連サーチャージを上乗せし始めた。

ただ配送会社の切り替えにはデメリットもあるとアナリストは指摘する。配送を複数社に分けると取扱量に応じた割引効果がなくなる可能性がある。また、年末商戦期の配送計画は数カ月前に決まるため、直前の変更は難しいという。ＪＰモルガンのアナリストは、アマゾンが近いうちにＵＰＳとフェデックスの市場支配を崩す可能性は低いとの見方を示した。

The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) was up 0.6% at 36,031.35 points as of 10:23 a.m. ET. Investors were also monitoring trade developments after US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he expected a [USN:L2N46B07T TEXT:"trade dispute with Canada"] to be resolved "soon" On the data front, Canadian [USN:S0N44B001 TEXT:"wholesale trade"] likely rose 0.5% in September from August, led by gains in machinery, equipment and motor vehicle-related sales, Statistics Canada said Among stocks, CAE (CAE.TO) rose 4.4% after the flight simulator maker [USN:L6N46C0RN TEXT:"agreed to sell"] Flightscape, its airline operations software business, to aviation technology firm SITA in a deal valued at $500 million, including debt

item.title: EQT to buy Range Resources in $13 billion deal to create top US gas producer
item.description: EQT said on Monday it will buy Range Resources in a $13 billion all-stock deal to create the largest US natural gas producer, betting on rising demand from LNG exports and power generation.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Saha
item.content:encoded: EQT (EQT.N) said on Monday it will buy Range Resources (RRC.N) in a $13 billion all-stock deal to create the largest US natural gas producer, betting on rising demand from LNG exports and power generation. The deal combines two major Appalachian Basin producers, giving EQT greater scale and infrastructure to serve utilities, LNG exporters and industrial customers. Including debt, the combined company will have an enterprise value of more than $50 billion. US natural gas consumption is expected to hit record highs, driven by LNG exports and power demand from AI data centers. The Energy Information Administration forecasts domestic consumption to rise from 91.9 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 94.3 bcfd in 2027. EQT now expects potential Appalachian gas demand rising to 25 bcfd, compared with its previous estimate of 20 bcfd, CEO Toby Rice said on a conference call. The combined company will have net production of more than 9 billion cubic feet equivalent per day (bcfed), over 30 years of drilling inventory across nearly 3 million net acres and more than 3,700 miles of midstream infrastructure. Rival Expand Energy (EXE.O) produced about 7.2 bcfed in 2025 and expects output of 7.4-7.6 bcfed in 2026. Range shareholders will receive 0.987 EQT shares per share held, valuing the deal at $12.83 billion, or $54.91 per share, a 20.6% premium to Friday's closing price, according to a Reuters calculation. Shares of EQT were down 2.3%, while those of Range Resources were up 16.7% at $53.14. EQT shareholders will own about 73% of the combined company, while Range investors will hold the remaining 27%. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. The combined company expects to generate about $20 billion in cumulative free cash flow over five years at recent market prices. The deal is also expected to lower EQT's unlevered free cash flow breakeven to below $2 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), helping it remain profitable through swings in natural gas prices. Rice said future production growth would be driven by customer demand rather than output targets, adding that mid-single-digit growth was achievable. EQT's management team will lead the combined company, which will retain its headquarters in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania. Two Range representatives, including CEO Dennis Degner, will join EQT's board.

item.title: Mankind Pharma's quarterly profit jumps 39% on strong chronic drug demand
item.description: Indian drugmaker Mankind Pharma reported an over 39% jump in second-quarter profit on Monday, helped by strong demand for chronic therapies such as diabetes and cardiac treatments,
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indian drugmaker Mankind Pharma (MNKI.NS) reported an over 39% jump in second-quarter profit on Monday, helped by strong demand for chronic therapies such as diabetes and cardiac treatments, Here are the details: Consolidated net profit rose to 7.11 billion rupees ($74.7 million) for the quarter ended September 30, from 5.12 billion rupees a year earlier. Mankind Pharma (MNKI.NS) and peers including Torrent Pharma (TORP.NS) continue to benefit from strong demand for chronic therapies, particularly diabetes and cardiovascular treatments, helping drive steady growth in the domestic formulations business. Its domestic revenue, excluding the consumer healthcare business, climbed 16% to 34.28 billion rupees, led by a 19% growth in its cardiac segment and a 16% climb in its anti-diabetes segment. This boosted overall revenue by 17.3% to 43.38 billion rupees. Mankind Pharma makes prescription medicines across chronic and acute therapies, and consumer healthcare products including Manforce condoms, Prega News pregnancy test kits and Gas-O-Fast antacid tablets. Last week, peer Torrent Pharma (TORP.NS) reported a [USN:L4N4690Z1 TEXT:"near 10% drop"] in quarterly profit as R&D costs outweighed strong domestic demand. ($1 = 95.2100 Indian rupees)

item.title: Exclusive-US political candidates tailor messages for AI models used by voters
item.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 26 : US political candidates have been engineering their campaign messages to appeal to the AI chatbots that more voters have been using to answer questions about issues, and documents seen by Reuters have revealed some of their strategies. One Powerpoint presentation proposed a strategy for
item.dc:creator: CNA

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 26 : US political candidates have been engineering their campaign messages to appeal to the AI chatbots that more voters have been using to answer questions about issues, and documents seen by Reuters have revealed some of their strategies.  One Powerpoint presentation proposed a strategy for Mike Minogue, Republican challenger to Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey. It aimed to convince ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other chatbots to present him as the preferred choice on key issues, and went well beyond traditional search-engine optimization that candidates have used for years. As AI increasingly becomes a source of news, political campaigns must make greater efforts to control its output and become its recommendation when voters ask questions such as who is best on issues like taxes, housing and public safety. Some experts worry about fact-checking and misinformation in AI campaigns. Fees can range from hundreds of dollars a month for small AI monitoring jobs to tens of thousands per month if consulting and buying media are included.

The presentation proposed that Minogue's campaign should create hundreds of AI-friendly policy pages and citations across the websites frequently cited by AI chatbots. It proposed ways to track how major chatbots respond to political questions, and systematically alter content until the answers reflect the candidate's platform. At the center of the pitch was the idea that in addition to persuading voters directly, campaigns can increasingly shape the information environment by feeding the internet, and AI assistants, data that influences how candidates are described, compared and recommended.  "Campaigns using AI-influence training are now a reality that we face and it will be ubiquitous by the 2028 cycle," which will include a presidential election, said Joe Bonilla, managing partner of Relentless Awareness. The New York-based creative strategy firm has worked with companies and political candidates at the federal, state, and local levels. "The public increasingly cannot and will not be able to discern what is created by systems like Claude and ChatGPT versus human-originated content," Bonilla said. The Powerpoint presentation prepared for Minogue's campaign and seen by Reuters describes generative engine optimization, or GEO, the AI-era successor to search engine optimization (SEO). It says the firm would buy placements on high-authority websites that AI models already cite. It would also produce YouTube and Reddit content and publish issue pages built to be picked up by chatbots. "When the campaign is ready, we run paid placements on high-domain-authority sites the LLMs (large language models) already cite — plus Reddit, which is disproportionately weighted in retrieval," the pitch deck says. VOTERS ASK CHATBOTS As online election information has surged, some 25 per cent of eligible voters have asked a chatbot about a political candidate when deciding how to vote, according to Cameron Hickey, CEO of the National Conference on Citizenship. "If you don't put the right information out there, who knows what the AI engines are going to grab onto," said Thomas Howell, CEO of Visigent, the Austin, Texas-based firm that wrote the strategy document for Minogue. Visigent has six political campaigns among its clients, but Howell would not identify his clients. The Minogue campaign did not return calls and emails requesting comment. Campaigns must now compete to become "the recommendation inside the AI answer" according to the presentation prepared for Minogue. "We are just at the beginning of this new era," said Meg Schwenzfeier with Caucus AI, which tracks voter usage of AI. "This year the focus has been on candidates ensuring their own websites surface in chatbot results," she said. But she warned "chatbots speak very authoritatively and can consume vast amounts of unvetted information, so we have to guard against misinformation."  FROM SEO TO GEO  Fees for AI strategists are tied to "AI recommendation share," meaning how often chatbots return the candidate in a response.  Visigent's website offers software for $134 a month and up to $9,000 monthly for large clients who require editorial design and development services. On the political side, Howell said fees start at $5,000 a month, but "if we also are going to be building paid media or paid placements or reaching out and doing any sort of influencer outreach or anything that is pay-for-play," fees could reach $50,000 a month. These fees are expected to rise, Howell said, as the 2028 presidential cycle kicks off after the midterm elections. The presentation shows the top success fee of $200,000 for a "category win." CampSight, another option geared toward progressive candidates, says it has helped younger candidates run for offices from school board to state legislature. CampSight, operated by Run for Something Action Fund, charges campaigns between $9 and $250 per month for information on what LLMs are saying about them and tips on influencing them. For statewide and federal campaigns pricing is "custom" and includes a "dedicated strategist." "When we started this project last summer, we were monitoring AI answers on some of our Run for Something candidates and we were seeing things that were said on Reddit appearing in AI answers the next day," Jordan Haines, the Run for Something Chief Technology Officer told Reuters. "This year, that dark fear hasn't really come to fruition. I think that the LLMs have been pretty savvy about discerning accurate and reputable information from non-reputable information." Run For Something's president Amanda Litman said in a post on X that dozens of campaigns use CampSight, with more than 300 candidates and organizations on its waiting list.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Fans and players revel on frozen pond of ice hockey nostalgia
item.description: The Winnipeg Jets have a modern indoor arena but tens of thousands of their fans and those of the visiting Montreal Canadiens zipped up parkas, pulled on warm hats and stuffed their hands into mittens to watch their teams battle in a temporarily converted outdoor Canadian football stadium.
item.dc:creator: Ed White
item.content:encoded: The Winnipeg Jets have a modern indoor arena but tens of thousands of their fans and those of the visiting Montreal Canadiens zipped up parkas, pulled on warm hats and stuffed their hands into mittens to watch their teams battle in a temporarily converted outdoor Canadian football stadium. Sunday night's Heritage Classic was not just something different for fans of the National Hockey League's rare but popular outdoor ice hockey celebrations. It was an invitation to indulge in memories and emotions of a type of ice hockey that has bound millions of people to the fast-moving, hard-hitting Canadian sport. The Classic is always played in Canada, usually every two-to-three years, but other outdoor games are played in the US. "It's hockey in its purest form," said Jets captain Adam Lowry a day before the game. "We grew up envisioning playing in the NHL when we were playing on outdoor rinks or on frozen ponds. It's where you spent countless hours with your friends." "Super-excited. So much fun. It brings back great memories," said Jets forward Kyle Connor, whose family's choice of home when he was young was based on having enough room in the back yard for a good rink. In front of a sellout crowd of 32,343 the Jets could not deliver a home win for their fans on Sunday night, but the thousands wearing red Canadiens jerseys were able to celebrate a 2-1 victory in a unique setting. OUTDOOR RESURGENCE Millions of rural Canadians and Americans grew up playing the sport on frozen ponds on the family farm. Many more grew up in cities playing on backyard rinks built by their parents encouraging their kids to dream of glory. The Classic is avowedly nostalgic. Sunday's iteration was designed to evoke the feeling of cabin life from decades ago, with the areas of the field not covered by the rink containing fire pits surrounded by Adirondack chairs, pond-themed mini-rinks, and images of ice hockey heritage. Outdoor ice hockey is far from fading in Canada. There has been a boom in front-yard hockey rink construction turning residential areas into places where the slap and boom of sticks hitting pucks into boards, the swooshing of skates and the cheers of goal-scoring are now commonplace in the winter months. This resurgence comes as ice hockey faces growing concerns about a drop in interest and participation numbers in Canada amid escalating costs of equipment and increasing popularity of other sports. Canadian[USN:L8N43705T TEXT:" success in international"] soccer and the rise of prominent Canadian players in basketball and other globally watched sports have given children competing sporting dreams. However, for superfans Jack Kostaniuk, 9, and his brother William, 7, the Heritage Classic was a chance to meet their heroes. "Hey buddy!" said Jets and Canadiens players as they fist-bumped the brothers on their way to the outdoor rink for a Saturday practice. Jack's dad, Tim, said "we love this," about the outdoor event. His children sometimes play on outdoor rinks and they are now getting to see their favorite players do the same. TURMOIL AND TRADE The Heritage Classic came at a time when the Jets needed a lift after months of upheaval. Goaltender Connor Hellebuyck, a key factor in Winnipeg's success in recent years, publicly questioned the team's direction following the 2025-26 season and was suspended by the club after he did not report to training camp. On Friday, the Jets traded him to the New Jersey Devils in a deal that brought several players and draft picks to Winnipeg. After arriving from the Devils, Dawson Mercer has had little time to get to know his new teammates before being thrust into the spotlight of the marquee outdoor game. Despite some jitters, he was excited about jumping in at the deep end of his new home. "It's going to be a fun time. My family is in town, so that'll be exciting and definitely more of a welcoming event," said Mercer. Also in town were throngs of Montreal fans, many of whom flew thousands of kilometers to sit outside at near-freezing temperatures to cheer on their team. A group of warmly dressed Montreal-born fans now living in southern Ontario told Reuters the only reason they came for this match was because it was being held outside, and that sounded cool.

item.title: Wall St rises as Anthropic's IPO filing sharpens focus on AI trade
item.description: Wall Street's main indexes edged up on Monday, led by advances in technology shares, while investors assessed Anthropic's IPO filing at the start of a week packed with corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision.
item.dc:creator: Shashwat Chauhan, Utkarsh Hathi
item.content:encoded: Wall Street's main indexes edged up on Monday, led by advances in technology shares, while investors assessed Anthropic's IPO filing at the start of a week packed with corporate earnings and the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision. Anthropic [USN:L3N46C10M TEXT:"disclosed"] steep losses and red-hot revenue growth in its filing for a US initial public offering, laying out its ambition to build AI systems capable of reshaping the global economy despite the high costs of developing the technology. The AI lab is pushing ahead with its listing plans even as a once-busy fall listing calendar has thinned out, with market volatility prompting companies to delay offerings. "It's a challenging environment, to say the least exactly when this IPO will take place, but there's a lot riding on not only the company, but the AI industry," said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth In Fairfield. Semiconductor and chip-related companies, widely viewed as some of the biggest winners of the AI boom, were leading the gains. The broader Philadelphia chips index (.SOX) was up around 1% after a turbulent few weeks. Anthropic's filing also arrived at a time when investors are increasingly scrutinizing the payoff from AI spending. About a third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, including hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , whose results would be [USN:L6N45T17Q TEXT:"closely watched for signs"] if the hefty AI investments are translating into growth. The focus follows a subdued reception to earnings from AI-linked megacaps last week. Meta (META.O) [USN:L6N468125 TEXT:"disappointed"] investors after raising its annual AI spending forecast again and said it would sell new stock to help pay for it, while Tesla (TSLA.O) also came under pressure after its [USN:L4N4671SD TEXT:"results"]. Meta said on Monday it [USN:L3N46C0RT TEXT:"plans to raise"] up to $95 billion in equity to fund its AI-related expansion of data centers, cloud computing power and other infrastructure. Its shares were last down 1.8%. The AI trade has come under pressure this month amid concerns that debt-funded spending may become harder to justify in the face of rising borrowing costs. Neocloud firm CoreWeave fell 2% and Nebius dipped 4.8% after Elon Musk [USN:L6N46B085 TEXT:"said"] in an X post markets have "almost entirely shut off access to money" for companies without substantial revenue independent of AI data centers, and predicted neocloud consolidation. At 09:55 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 236.42 points, or 0.45%, to 52,451.58. The S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 43.20 points, or 0.57%, to 7,666.88, while the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) edged up 119.43 points, or 0.46%, at 26,074.96. Market breadth was strong, with 10 of the 11 S&P 500 sectors trading higher. Consumer discretionary (.SPLRCD) and industrials (.SPLRCI) led the gains. Megacap and growth stocks were mixed. Tesla (TSLA.O) jumped 5.9% to a more than three-month high after Barclays upgraded its rating on the stock to "overweight" from "equal-weight". Crude oil prices eased after hitting a near six-month high last week. On Sunday, [USN:S8N43E021 TEXT:"Qatari mediators"] traveled to Tehran as part of an effort to de-escalate regional tensions in coordination with the United States. Elsewhere, the Fed's rate decision is due on Wednesday, with a pause widely expected after its September raise. Traders still see a December hike as firmly possible, and at least two 25-basis-point increases by mid-2027, according to LSEG data. Both the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures index for September, and third-quarter GDP, expected to show 3.2% growth, are due on Thursday. Investors are also monitoring the November 3 midterm elections , which will decide control of the US Congress. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.73-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.25-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted three new 52-week highs and three new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 44 new highs and 180 new lows.

item.title: US retailers face record holiday delivery prices from surcharges tied to costlier diesel
item.description: The most expensive parcel shipping year on record is on track to end with the highest-ever holiday season delivery prices as soaring diesel prices drive even higher fuel surcharge rates from UPS and FedEx , boosting costs for retailers.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Baertlein
item.content:encoded: The most expensive parcel shipping year on record is on track to end with the highest-ever holiday season delivery prices as soaring diesel prices drive even higher fuel surcharge rates from UPS (UPS.N) and FedEx (FDX.N) , boosting costs for retailers. Holiday-related package volume can double during the fourth quarter, when pricing for ground deliveries, including e-commerce purchases, is expected to be 5.8% higher than the same period last year, according to the TD Cowen/AFS Freight Index. Pricing for speedier express parcel deliveries is forecast to jump 13.8% from the fourth quarter of 2025, according to the index, which analyzes anonymized data from 1,800 shippers including major retailers. The index reports percentage change rather than dollar amounts because parcel costs vary based on weight, size and destination. "Fuel is front and center in everybody's consideration and, again, no real good news there," said Mingshu Bates, chief analytics officer at AFS Logistics. The US average on-highway diesel price was $6.28 per gallon as of October 19, according to the Energy Information Administration, up 65% since the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28. CHANGES TO CARRIERS' CALCULATIONS BOOST COSTS But diesel price increases account for just under 30% of the fuel surcharge cost, Bates said. Surcharges driven by changes to how industry leaders such as UPS and FedEx calculate them are rising far faster than fuel prices — and go up even when fuel prices do not, she said. For example, when diesel was $2.91 per gallon in the first quarter of 2021, the index fuel surcharge was 7.75% of the base shipping rate. Even if diesel returned to that price, the fuel surcharge now would be 23.75%, roughly three times higher, according to the index. That reflects how changes in fuel surcharge calculations are raising carriers' revenue and driving up retailers' costs. Based on company surcharge tables at the EIA's average diesel price of $6.28, UPS' fuel surcharge is 29.5% and FedEx's is 29%. UPS said its pricing reflects its premium service and infrastructure investments. FedEx did not immediately comment. The companies will report quarterly earnings this week and investors are keen to learn if customers are pushing back on surcharges. Fast-growing delivery firms, including OnTrac, GoFo, UniUni, Jitsu and Veho, cover some 70% of the US population and have added capacity to handle more volume during the holiday season, said Satish Jindel, president of ShipMatrix, a delivery tracking and management firm. "They are getting adoption from many shippers looking to lower their transportation spend," Jindel said. Nevertheless, some of those companies have also adopted hefty fuel surcharges. OnTrac's West Coast surcharge is 29.5% for the week ending October 25, according to the company's publicly available surcharge table. Retailers and other delivery customers could save money by shifting their business to the US Postal Service or to Amazon.com's (AMZN.O) logistics arm. The heavily regulated USPS imposed its first fuel surcharge of 8% on most packages in April, the same month Amazon began adding a 3.5% fuel and logistics-related surcharge to sellers' fulfillment fees. Switching deliveries between companies can bring downsides, analysts said. Splitting deliveries between firms can nullify any savings based on volume and holiday delivery plans are set months ahead, making late changes difficult, they said. To that end, JPMorgan analysts said it is unlikely Amazon will soon break UPS and FedEx's grip on the market.

item.title: Beware a boring UK budget that ages badly
item.description: Chancellor John Healey has talked markets into expecting little this autumn. Amid a £10 bln fiscal hole created by the Iran crisis, he may defer thorny spending decisions to 2027. But past budgets show how a calm reception can sour later, highlighting the risk of delay.
item.dc:creator: Jon Sindreu
item.content:encoded: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s ability to craft a narrative is on full display. To voters, he pitched radical policy changes addressing living costs and shifting decision-making locally. To "bond vigilantes," he looks to have sold a boring budget where little will be announced on October 28. The problem with plot holes is that criticism pours in later, when people mull them over. Burnham's finance minister John Healey is facing the same challenges as his predecessor Rachel Reeves. Her fiscal rules, designed to avoid a Liz Truss-style bond market revolt required day-to-day spending to balance and debt to fall relative to GDP years down the line. Yet after an initial high-tax budget in 2024, low growth made the "headroom" of £10 billion she had left over the deficit rule look paltry. She was forced not only to plug the gap by promising more revenue increases and spending cuts, but to raise it to £24 billion. Today, the situation has worsened again. The Iran war has pushed up borrowing costs, eating into those numbers. But based on what Healey has suggested, analysts don't expect him to rebuild the headroom, which is expected to come in between £10 billion and £15 billion on budget day. The fact that 10-year gilt yields have headed lower over the past two weeks implies the City of London also sees an energy shock as reasonable justification to eat into the cushion. Bank of America analysts break it down. Living-cost measures already announced by Burnham — including frozen bus fares and a 5% VAT cut on electricity — amount to £2 billion this fiscal year, and similar policies costing £13 billion until March 2028 could join them. Add £5 billion for defence over four years. That all means Healey may raise taxes by as much as £19 billion, Bank of America reckons, with banks likely among the targets. But compared to Reeves’ 2024 budget, designed to raise £40 billion annually, it's small potatoes. The budget may strike a balance consistent with Burnham's pattern of pairing large ambitions with low-key policies. But tough decisions will likely be kicked into the long grass. Tax increases are expected from 2028 onwards, and there's little indication so far that the Treasury is rushing to tackle much-needed welfare reform. Furthermore, Burnham has not yet spelled out how he will fund his plans to provide Brits with more old-age care. A bigger problem is that the current fiscal math contains a lot of unspecified back-loaded belt tightening. Government departments were already set to increase inflation-adjusted spending by only 1.3% yearly until 2031, compared to 2.5% over the past decade. Add the recent cost surge and it falls to 1%. Government hopes that productivity gains will fill the gap look extremely optimistic. Healey can avoid details for now, but he must still explain how exactly they are supposed to happen in the Spending Review next year. Market sentiment can be a double-edged sword. Healey should remember that, even if a budget initially gets the green light from investors, they can later reassess the whole affair. This is exactly what happened to Reeves, who initially got a warm reception to her 2024 budget only to scramble to cater to investors' narrow focus on the shrinking headroom in 2025. Storytelling is ultimately no replacement for credible plans. Follow Jon Sindreu on X and LinkedIn . British Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey is due to present the government's Autumn Budget on October 28. Rising European oil and gas prices have raised concerns that higher energy-related spending and weaker growth could reduce the Treasury's fiscal headroom against its borrowing rules. Official data published on October 21 showed that public sector borrowing in the year to September was £97.8 billion, which is 4.3% less than in the same period of last year but 6.5% more than was expected by the United Kingdom's independent fiscal watchdog, the Office for Budget Responsibility, in its March forecasts. The UK government will issue debt to give £20.4 billion of additional support to the National Wealth Fund (NWF) and British Business Bank (BBB), the Financial Times published on October 24 citing the Treasury. As of 0900 GMT on October 26, Britain's 10-year government bond yields traded at 5.3588%, compared with 5.3656% at the close on October 23. Most benchmark yields from peer countries were up at the time. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: Officials from Mecca pact countries to meet Iranian officials in Tehran
item.description: This will be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the wider Iran conflict.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Officials from Mecca pact countries to meet Iranian officials in Tehran

This will be the first high-level contact between Iran and all members of the three-nation bloc since Saudi Arabia was drawn deeper into the wider Iran conflict.

FILE PHOTO: Turkey's Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, Turkey's Defence Minister Yasar Guler, Turkish Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu, Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif, Saudi Arabia's Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Saudi Arabia's Chief of General Staff General Fayyadh bin Hamed Al-Ruwaili and Pakistan's retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood, Secretary General of the Mecca defence pact, take part in the Mecca defense pact meeting between Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, October 5, 2026. Saudi Press Agency/Handout via REUTERS/File Photo
